title: X0 hardware gate (Qwen3.6-27B, 2x H100 box): does the new box reproduce one 23 Oct necessity cell?
command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py parts --name x0_hw_gate_parts_27b --map d1_topics2_map_27b --why "X0 hardware gate: one 23 Oct cell (bridge_word:16) rerun on the 2x H100 box" --lo 16 --sets bridge_word --force bridge_word:16 && uv run python scripts/x0_hw_gate.py --new x0_hw_gate_parts_27b --ref d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2 --cell bridge_word:16
question: Does the new box (2x H100 80GB PCIe, x86_64, driver CUDA 12.8) reproduce, read for read, a cell the 23 Oct necessity run (d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2, A100) measured: the bridge's word at layer 16, both readers, the same scenes, map, lens and code path?
why_it_matters: X0 compares its numbers with the 23 Oct ones and is the gate for the week. A hardware or kernel difference that flips reads would be confounded with the effect.

hypotheses.H-same: the reads agree on >= 97% of rows without random draws. Prior: none set (an agreement check, not a claim)
hypotheses.H-differs: the agreement is below 97%: X0 does not start; the disagreeing rows are reported

decision_rule: Fixed 24 Oct before the run (hardware addendum v2: "rerun one 23 Oct cell, item agreement at least 97%"). Rows are matched on item, set, layer, part, source and null flag (scripts/x0_hw_gate.py). The gate covers the rows whose arm draws no random tensor: full, lens2, not_lens2, jspace, not_jspace, jspace_wo_own and not_jspace_matched, non-null, both readers. PASS iff the share of those rows whose read role (b / A / other) matches the 23 Oct row is >= 0.97. Otherwise FAIL: the script exits 3, so the X0 jobs that depend on this one do not start. Arms drawing random tensors (rand_omp, rand_sub, not_rand_sub, the matched pieces, every null; drawn on CUDA in this code) are reported per part, not gated. The median |ld| difference is reported per group.
controls: the reference run itself: the same code path (statement_positions.py, exp04_brew_parts.py, suite_split.py, tasks_v2.py, suite_v1.py and src/bridge_jspace/ have no diff between c2e31c9, the reference run's commit, and this commit)
the random-draw arms reported beside the gate
n: 180 scenes x 2 readers (PP, PM) of d1_topics_v2, one cell (bridge_word:16), 7784 rows in the reference
notes: The reference ran on the A100 box at c2e31c9 (dirty tree; the parts code path has no diff since). Inputs are committed: results/statement_positions/d1_topics2_map_27b, results/tasks_v2/d1_topics2_competence_27b, results/statement_positions/d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2. GPU0, first job of the queue (hardware addendum v2). Timing basis: the reference's 8 cells took ~1.3 h on one A100; one cell is ~10 min.

question: At the 27B's layer 32, at the asked person's bridge word in the org run (chat), split by whether the bridge's locker sentence comes before or after the asked pick sentence: can a linear probe read (a) the lookup's answer digit, (b) the index of the sentence holding the bridge's locker, (c) the bridge's identity (positive control), above the majority and chance baselines?
why_it_matters: X0 says the 27B and 9B lookups flip mostly in locker-before scenes and do not need the J++ part (9B) or need more atoms of it (27B); the digit check found no digit route. The probes ask what the word holds instead: the answer value itself, or an address of where it is.

hypotheses.H-value: (a) high in locker-before and at chance in locker-after: the answer value is stored at the word, not in J++ form. Prior: none set (descriptive, after data; Dan's reading)
hypotheses.H-address: (b) high in locker-before with (a) at chance: the word stores an address (a lookback-style pointer). Prior: none set (Dan's reading)

decision_rule: Descriptive, added after data, not part of X0's rule (Dan, 24 Oct evening). Linear probes (one-hot ridge, standardized features, penalty by inner 4-fold CV) on h_org at the bridge's word, layer 32; (a) and (b) cross-validated by bridge entity (5 folds, entities held out), (c) by item (5 folds, entities spread: a held-out entity is an unseen class). Per target and stratum (locker before / after / both): accuracy against chance (1 / classes) and the training folds' majority class; for (b) also the structure-only baseline (the agent's addition: the most frequent locker index given the asked pick's sentence index). 95% CIs from a cluster bootstrap over bridge entities (10,000 resamples, seed 0); probe - best baseline on the same draws. Primary: the 200 X0 items of x0_necessity_27b_chat; secondary: every chat scene of d1_topics_v3. Reading (Dan, before the run): (a) high before and at chance after -> value at the word; (b) high before with (a) at chance -> address.
controls: locker-after scenes: the locker sentence follows the word, so (a) and (b) cannot be read from it there (control by construction)
the bridge identity probe (positive control: the pipeline reads what the word surely holds)
majority-class and chance baselines, cross-validated; the structure-only baseline for (b)
n: 200 X0 items (101 locker-before, 99 locker-after; 38 / 33 entities) and every chat scene of d1_topics_v3 (600)
notes: Order (Dan, 24 Oct evening): after the single-change alt, before the 122B. Cost: one model load, 600 forwards (~10 min). States saved fp16 in results (states.npz, ~6 MB), so further probes are CPU-only.

question: On the single-change items (x0_single_27b_r2 at L32, qwen35_9b_x0_single_r2 at L12; locker-before primary), with P the probe-(b) subspace (the decision directions of a linear probe for the index of the bridge's locker sentence, fit on fresh d1_topics_v4 org states, locker-before; rank = classes - 1): (1) does removing PΔ from the bridge edit cost the lookup more flips than removing a random part of the same share, while the recall loses no more than with the random part? (2) does PΔ alone flip the lookup more than the random part alone?
why_it_matters: The probe reads the address (which sentence holds the bridge's locker) at the bridge's word in locker-before scenes, and not the answer digit. If the lookup acts on the bridge through that address, removing it should cost the lookup, not the recall; keeping only it should carry the lookup's flips. Expected direction (Dan): the lookup loses flips, the recall does not.

hypotheses.H-lookup: lookup: probe dependence - random dependence > 0 (lower CI > 0), locker-before. Prior: Dan's, predictions batch 27
hypotheses.H-recall: recall: probe dependence - random dependence <= 0.10. Prior: Dan's, batch 27
hypotheses.H-sufficiency: lookup: S_probe_only / S_whole - S_rand_only / S_whole > 0 (lower CI > 0). Prior: Dan's, batch 27

decision_rule: Descriptive, added after data (Dan, 24 Oct ~18:45, item 6). Per model, reader and locker order: S for whole, no_probe (Δ - PΔ), no_rand (Δ minus X0's random-subspace part at PΔ's share), probe_only (PΔ), rand_only (the random part alone, the agent's matched control); probe dependence 1 - S_no_probe / S_whole against the random one (excess, paired), and S_probe_only / S_whole against S_rand_only / S_whole (paired); 95% CIs from a cluster bootstrap over bridge entities (10,000 resamples, seed 0); top-token read, both readers on the identical patch. Locker-before is primary; locker-after descriptive (lookups rarely flip there). Results not opened or summarized before Dan's batch-27 commit.
controls: the random-subspace part at PΔ's share (removal) and the random part alone (sufficiency)
both readers on the identical patch
the probe trained on fresh scenes (d1_topics_v4), disjoint from the test items (d1_topics_v3)
n: the 200 single-change items per model (~100 locker-before)
notes: One 2-GPU job, two processes (27B on GPU0, 9B on GPU1). Depends on x0_probe_power (its states train P). The run also saves h_org, Δ and the J++ parts of Δ at k = 25 and 100 per item (states.npz), for Dan's items 2 and 3 (the probe on h_alt and on patched states, CPU). Cost: 200 items x 6 reads x 2 readers + OMP at k = 100: ~15 min per model.

question: On the single-change items (x0_single_27b_r2 at L32, qwen35_9b_x0_single_r2 at L12), both readers: how many flips are lost when Δ loses (w) its least-squares fit on the J++ directions of the org and alt bridge tokens and their one-token surface variants, (jw) its 25-atom J++ part with those variants banned, (pca) its 25-atom part over the top 2,000 principal directions of the layer (200 held-out d1_topics_v4 prompts, every token), and (jpp) X0's J++ part, each against a random part of its own share?
why_it_matters: The J++ part is mostly not the bridge word (the bridge's tokens are in the top 25 atoms of 28 of 40 items, ~12% of the part), so "the bridge's word form" is not shown. This separates the word from J++ beyond the word, and J++ from any direction the layer favours.

hypotheses.H-word: recall's loss mostly in w. Prior: Dan's, predictions batch 27
hypotheses.H-beyond: recall's loss mostly in jw, with pca inert. Prior: Dan's, batch 27
hypotheses.H-geometry: pca about as large as jpp for recall. Prior: Dan's, batch 27

decision_rule: Descriptive, added after data (Dan's audit, 24 Oct ~19:30, item 2). Per model, reader and part: median share of ||Δ||², S_whole, S_no, S_noRand, Jdep, Rdep, excess (X0's cells; cluster bootstrap over bridge entities, 10,000 resamples, seed 0), top-token read, both readers on the identical patch. Reading (Dan): recall's loss mostly in w -> the word form; mostly in jw with pca inert -> J-space beyond the word; pca about as large as J++ -> "J++-specific" means "aligned with the layer's geometry", and the README must say so. title: Batch 45, 45b on the 9B (L12): where is the binding made when the locker comes after the pick? Bridge-word change at L, L/2, L/4; S patched into O at the locker sentences at L and L/2
command: BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP= uv run python scripts/x45b_binding.py run --name qwen35_9b_x45b_binding --why "batch 45, test 45b (jobs/c3/batch45.yaml): the 9B at L12; (a) the bridge-word change at L, (b) at L/2 and L/4, (c) S patched into O at every locker-sentence token at L, (d) at L/2; S read on S"
examples_command: BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b uv run python scripts/x45b_binding.py examples --name qwen35_9b_x45b_binding
question: In the main test's scenes where the original bridge's locker sentence comes after the asked pick, is the binding made at the locker sentences rather than at the bridge word: does patching S's states into O at every token of the locker sentences (at L or L/2) switch at least half of the lookups that S itself switches, while the bridge-word change at L switches at most 0.25?
why_it_matters: In these scenes the bridge-word change switches few lookups (x0_strata, 24 Oct: 0.19 on the 9B at L12, 0.09 on the 27B at L32, against 0.86 / 0.76 where the locker comes first), although S itself switches them all. If the model can only bind the pick to its locker once it reads the locker sentence, the change lives at the locker sentences, and the lookup's low rate there is about reading order, not about the bridge word.

hypotheses.Q45.5: The reading-order explanation holds: (a) yes; (b) no. Dan's answer in docs/predictions_batch45.md (Q45.5), committed before any result of this test is opened.

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (batch 45, jobs/c3/batch45.yaml, 45b): the reading-order explanation holds if (c) or (d) switches at least half of the lookups that S itself switches, while (a) stays at or below 0.25. As implemented (scripts/x45b_binding.py, rule): the lookup, point estimates; "half of the lookups S switches" = among the items whose lookup S read on S switches, the share (c) (or (d)) switches >= 0.5; (a) = its switch rate over all the items <= 0.25; can't tell if S switches none. Switch = the top token at the read step is S's answer's first token (X0's chat read). Rates with cluster-bootstrap CIs over bridge items (10,000 resamples, seed 0) and the n.
controls: (a) the bridge-word change at L: the main test's whole arm rerun on these items (stored 0.19 on the 9B, x0_strata); checked against the stored reads of qwen35_9b_x0_necessity (a at L12, b_half at L6)
S read on S: what S itself switches (the rule's reference); checked against the stored S read (competence.jsonl)
O unedited (arm none): reads O's answer
the recall read on the identical patches (descriptive)
n: the 100 items of qwen35_9b_x0_necessity (chat, L12) whose org locker sentence comes after the asked pick, 28 bridge entities; all 100 align token for token between O and S (plan stage, 26 Oct)
notes: Results stay closed until docs/predictions_batch45.md holds Dan's Q45.5 commit: the job runs the run and examples stages only; the verdict after that commit, on the CPU: BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b uv run python scripts/x45b_binding.py verdict --name qwen35_9b_x45b_binding. Locker sentences = every 'The locker of <thing> is <n>.' sentence of the context (3 per scene; one that comes before the first changed pick has h_S = h_O, a no-op). L/2 = 6, L/4 = 3. est_gpu_hours from the timing ledger (H100 PCIe): qwen35_9b_x0_single_r2 took 612 s for about ten times this run's forwards (competence on 600 scenes and 8 layers of reads), qwen35_9b_x0_probe 87 s (load and a few hundred forwards); this run: 100 items x (2 recorded forwards + 2 readers x (one 6-row read of O + one read of S)) + 10 example items' greedy tokens, about 3 minutes.

As computed (x6_routes.first_locker_rule): the lookup's position share with only the pointer part (keep_alf) on the C2 scenes whose pointer move (the O bridge's locker slot -> the S bridge's) involves slot 0, the base scenes every variant has (paired); a variant cuts if its point estimate is <= 0.5 x V0's and the paired cluster-bootstrap 95% CI of V0 minus it has lower bound > 0; within = |variant - V0| <= 0.10 on the point estimates; if both rules hold (possible when V0 <= 0.2) the first is reported and flagged; a variant that misses its gate makes the verdict "not tested". decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch45.yaml, 45k, with its overrides). "Identity route is lens-readable on the 27B" if on the 27B, from k = 25 to k = 100, identity answers in C2 fall by at least 0.2 more than with the random part, while position answers fall by less than 0.1 (or rise); and on the 9B neither falls by at least 0.1. "Pointer becomes lens-readable on the 27B" if position answers in C2 fall by at least 0.2 more than with the random part, and the k = 100 span's mean cos^2 with U is at least 0.5. "Generic fitting" if jpp_other at k = 100 costs the 27B lookup at least 2/3 of what this scene's J++ costs (override 2: read on the main test, job x45k_generic_27b against results/x0_necessity/x0_kmatch_27b; the routes jpp_other arm in this job is descriptive). Otherwise "can't tell". Report all four per model. As computed (fixed before the run): "fall from k = 25 to k = 100 by at least x more than with the random part" = [share(no_jpp25) - share(no_jpp100)] - [share(no_jpp25_rand) - share(no_jpp100_rand)] >= x, C2 lookup route shares, point estimates (paired cluster-bootstrap CIs beside them); "position falls by less than 0.1 (or rises)" = the same difference for position < 0.1; the 9B clause: both identity's and position's difference < 0.1. Mean cos^2 with U = per C2 item ||P_span(atoms) U||_F^2 / rank(U), averaged over the items; with the identity direction, ||P_span(atoms) u||^2 / ||u||^2. "Costs the lookup" = the lookup's extra loss (switches lost without the part minus without its random part, over the whole change's switches). Each label is evaluated per model. Overrides (Dan ~22:05): 1. precondition: the 27B's C0 lookup extra loss at k = 100 (no_jpp100 vs its random part) is reported; below 0.2, Q45.9 is "can't tell: the main-test curve does not reproduce in routes scenes", whatever the other clauses say; 3. precedence for Q45.9: "Generic fitting" if it holds, otherwise the labels that hold on the 27B, otherwise "can't tell". Code: x6_routes.jppk_rule per run, jppk-summary over the runs (x6_routes.jppk_labels; generic_rule on the main test). no_jpp25 is the existing no_jpp arm (signed OMP, k = 25); thresholds with a 1e-9 tolerance (a value exactly at a bar counts as at it). Gates as the routes test (read accuracy 0.80; C0 within 0.10 of the 9B's reference). Cluster bootstrap over the bridge item, 10,000 resamples, seed 0.

title: Batch 45k on Muse L26 (if time): why does the lookup lose with more J++ atoms? The sanity swap (C0) and another item moved (C2) with J++ removed at 25, 50 and 100 atoms and another scene's 100 atoms refit here, each against a random part of its share; the atoms' overlap with the pointer and the identity direction
command: BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP= uv run python scripts/x6_routes.py run --name muse30b_x6_routes_x45k_r3 --conditions C0,C2 --jpp-ks 25 50 100 --jpp-other --c0-min 0.5
question: On the 27B the main test's lookup extra loss grows with the J++ atoms (0.12 / 0.30 / 0.60 at k = 25 / 50 / 100; about 0 on the other models). Do the extra atoms take out the identity route, the pointer, or any fitted directions?
why_it_matters: The 9B's J++ part at k = 100 holds more of the change (44%) than the 27B's (31%), so "removed too much" does not explain the curve. Which route the lookup loses as k grows, and how much the k atoms overlap the pointer and the identity direction, tell a lens-readable route from overfitting.

hypotheses.H-batch45: Q45.9 (45k) in predictions/2026-10-26_dan.md (section Batch 45), committed by Dan before any 45k code or run (8025b808); overrides (Dan ~22:05) committed before any 45k job (1fad1c34)

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch45.yaml, 45k, with its overrides). "Identity route is lens-readable on the 27B" if on the 27B, from k = 25 to k = 100, identity answers in C2 fall by at least 0.2 more than with the random part, while position answers fall by less than 0.1 (or rise); and on the 9B neither falls by at least 0.1. "Pointer becomes lens-readable on the 27B" if position answers in C2 fall by at least 0.2 more than with the random part, and the k = 100 span's mean cos^2 with U is at least 0.5. "Generic fitting" if jpp_other at k = 100 costs the 27B lookup at least 2/3 of what this scene's J++ costs (override 2: read on the main test, job x45k_generic_27b against results/x0_necessity/x0_kmatch_27b; the routes jpp_other arm in this job is descriptive). Otherwise "can't tell". Report all four per model. As computed (fixed before the run): "fall from k = 25 to k = 100 by at least x more than with the random part" = [share(no_jpp25) - share(no_jpp100)] - [share(no_jpp25_rand) - share(no_jpp100_rand)] >= x, C2 lookup route shares, point estimates (paired cluster-bootstrap CIs beside them); "position falls by less than 0.1 (or rises)" = the same difference for position < 0.1; the 9B clause: both identity's and position's difference < 0.1. OMP with K = 100 on the change; without atoms 26-100 (1-25 kept), without 1-25, without 1-100, each against a random part of its share, and 75 random lens atoms at the 26-100 share; routes (another item moved, 300) and the main test (200), both readers

question: Where does the lookup's identity route live: in lens atoms beyond the 25 the recall uses, or outside the lens? Without OMP atoms 26-100 of the change (atoms 1-25 kept), do the lookup's identity answers fall beyond a random part of the same share, while the recall barely loses?
why_it_matters: Fig 2b(b): on the 27B, removing 100 J++ atoms cuts identity answers from 0.66 to under 0.10 while a random part of the same share leaves ~0.70; at 25 atoms the lookup barely moves. So "around the lens" on the 27B may mean "outside the recall's 25 atoms, inside the lens's wider span". Removing atoms 26-100 alone separates the two readings.

hypotheses.Q47.1: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q47.1, per model: 27B; 9B; Muse); not committed when this spec was written, so the job is sealed: per-item outputs only, no verdict; scripts/x47_atoms.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed, and x6_routes' / x0_necessity's own verdict and examples stages refuse these runs too.

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.1), verbatim: "On routes scenes, for identity answers; on the main test, for extra loss: (a) "the lookup's identity route sits in lens atoms beyond the recall's 25": without 26-100, identity answers fall >= 0.30 beyond the random part (paired CI excluding 0) and the recall's extra loss without 26-100 is <= 0.10, on >= 2 of 3 models; (b) "continuum": both readers lose >= 0.20 beyond random without 26-100; (c) "outside the lens": without 26-100, identity answers fall < 0.10 beyond random (then the 27B's K = 100 loss is a size effect of the whole removal, and the 27B stays "misses the strict rule, cause not found"). Report each slice's share of the change." As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the run): OMP = X0's signed OMP over the J++ lens's letter-token atoms at L (x0_necessity.fit; x0_parts.omp_atoms gives the same picks in order, so atoms 1-25 are the k = 25 picks). On the change Δ = h_S - h_O at the bridge word: "remove 1-25" = Δ minus P25 Δ (the existing J++ k = 25 arm); "remove 1-100" = Δ minus P100 Δ; "remove 26-100 only (keep 1-25)" = Δ minus (P100 Δ - P25 Δ), what atoms 26-100 add beyond atoms 1-25 (their span projected off atoms 1-25), so P25 Δ is kept exactly and the 1-25 and 26-100 removals add up to the 1-100 removal. "The random part" of each = Δ's projection on the first k columns of X0's random basis (seed 888 + L), k per item matching that part's share of ||Δ||^2 (statement_positions.random_subspace_part). Random lens atoms (dumbest way 2, count and share matched): per item 75 letter-token lens atoms drawn uniformly outside its 100 OMP picks (seed 4701 and the scene id); their part = Δ's component in their span projected off atoms 1-25 (as the 26-100 slice), scaled to the 26-100 slice's share of ||Δ||^2 (alpha per item reported; alpha > 1 where they hold less); also unscaled, at its own share, against its own random part (descriptive). "Identity answers fall beyond the random part" (routes C2, lookup) = identity share without the random part of 26-100's share minus identity share without 26-100, the identity share being the share of the C2 items whose top token at X0's chat read is the identity route's digit (x6_routes.classify); "paired CI excluding 0" = its paired cluster-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0. "The recall's extra loss without 26-100" (main test: two people swap picks, d1_topics_v3, chat, L) = X0's excess, [1 - S(without 26-100) / S(whole)] - [1 - S(without its random part) / S(whole)], S the recall's switch rate (top token = the changed answer's first token). (b)'s "both readers lose >= 0.20 beyond random" = the lookup's identity fall (routes) >= 0.20 and the recall's extra loss (main test) >= 0.20, each reader on its scene set as in (a); the lookup's main-test extra loss is reported beside. Per model: (a) if the identity fall >= 0.30, its lower bound > 0 and the recall's extra loss <= 0.10; (b) if the identity fall >= 0.20 and the recall's extra loss >= 0.20; (c) if the identity fall < 0.10; else "none of (a)-(c)" (the bars make the three exclusive). Q47.1's answer per model is that label; (a) for the batch holds on >= 2 of 3 models (9B, 27B, Muse). Gates: the routes test's read gate on C2 (O unedited, 0.80 per reader) and X0's on the main test (0.80 per reader, >= 150 eligible); a failed routes gate = "not tested"; a failed main-test gate or an invalid recall cell (X0: whole-change switch rate < 0.30 or < 30 switches) leaves (a) and (b) "can't tell" while (c) is still read. Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9 at the bars); paired cluster-bootstrap CIs over the bridge items (10,000 resamples, seed 0) beside them. Reported beside: every arm's route shares; each part's fall beyond its random part (identity, position, value); 26-100 against the random atoms at its share (paired); each slice's share of ||Δ||^2 per item and its median (1-25, 26-100, 1-100; the random atoms' own share and alpha); the 26-100 vs 1-25 check (dumbest way 1: items where 26-100 holds more than 1-25; items where per atom it holds less); the mean cos^2 with U (dumbest way 3: ||P U||_F^2 / rank U, U the pointer directions fit on fresh scenes, not refit) of the spans of atoms 1-25, 1-100, the 26-100 slice and the random atoms. Code: scripts/x47_atoms.py verdict (model_label, batch_rule).
controls: every part against a random part of the same share of ||Δ||^2 (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L)

random lens atoms (dumbest way 2): 75 letter-token lens atoms per item outside its 100 OMP picks (seed 4701 + scene id), projected off atoms 1-25, scaled to the 26-100 share; unscaled at their own share against its random part (descriptive)
without atoms 1-25 and without 1-100, each against its random part (the existing arms, rerun in the same job)
the recall on the identical patch (routes: its S-answer share; main test: extra loss)
per item: each slice's share of the change (dumbest way 1) and the spans' cos^2 with U (dumbest way 3)

why_it_matters: The lookup goes around the lens through the pointer. Whether the pointer is merely unread by the lens or also inexpressible in its atoms decides the README's monitoring bullet; the sanity swap (J++ and U removed together leave 0.45 / 0.53 / 0.74 of lookups) answers the other reading (augment the lens with the pointer).

question: In six-locker scenes, is the pointer's order code ordinal (a line over slots that one shift vector moves along), categorical (first locker vs the rest), or slot-specific (binding IDs: pairwise moves work, no common shift)?
why_it_matters: The pointer marks the first locker in a clean three-locker layout; the 2nd-vs-3rd removal found no separate direction, yet writing mu_3 - mu_2 moves the lookup at 2x. Three lockers cannot tell "first vs rest" from "a line over slots". Ordinal = a positional line the lens cannot read (Dai et al. 2024's ordering subspace); categorical = a one-bit marker; slot-specific = binding IDs (Feng & Steinhardt 2023).

title: Batch 48.3 on the 9B (L12): why locker-after lookups ignore the bridge word. Which person picked the item, probed at the locker sentence's item and number tokens (locker-after vs locker-first); the person contrast's J++ share; the contrast written at another person's locker sentence, read by the lookup and the recall
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x48_bind.py run --name qwen35_9b_x48_bind --why "batch 48, test 48.3 (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml; Q48.3): states at every locker sentence's item and number tokens of the main-test and 45m scenes at L12 (the probe is fit at the verdict), the person mass-mean contrast fit on half the bridge entities, its J++ k = 25 share beside random directions', and s (mu_asked - mu_picker) at s = 1, 2 written at another person's locker sentence on the other half, against a random vector of the same norm; both readers; sealed"
question: In locker-after scenes, is the person -> item binding made forward at the locker sentence, outside the lens: can a probe read which of the scene's three people picked the item at the locker sentence's item / number token (and not where the sentence precedes the pick), does the person contrast sit outside the J++ part, and does writing the asked person's contrast at another person's locker sentence send the lookup to that sentence's locker? Does the recall move with it?
why_it_matters: The account (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml) says that when the locker comes after the pick the binding is made forward at the locker sentence, so the bridge word is not read at L there (hence the lookup's low switch rate under the bridge-word change in locker-after scenes); a write at the locker sentence that redirects the lookup, with the probe and the lens share, tests that part of the account directly. Whether the recall moves too says whether the sentence binds the locker address only or the whole "Iris's pick = frog".

The probe: which of the scene's three people (the generator's pickers, by name) picked the item, a ridge probe (x0_probe's, one-hot over the training rows' names, the prediction the best-scoring of the scene's three names, chance 1/3), fit at the verdict on the stored states with the sentence's item held out (5 folds, entities shuffled by seed 0), trained and scored within each stratum (after: the sentence follows its picker's pick; before: it precedes it); the rule's cells are the asked item's sentence in locker-after and in locker-first scenes, every locker sentence with a picker reported beside, and the after-trained probe on the before states ("transfer"). title: Batch 48.5 on the 9B (L12): the recall's second route. 45m's locker-first scenes; at the bridge token the change without its J++ part, plus the pointer write 2 (mu_k - mu_j) to each other locker slot k; the write alone; the no-J++ change plus a random vector of the write's norm. command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x48_route2.py run --name qwen35_9b_x48_route2 --why "batch 48, test 48.5 (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml; Q48.5): on 45m's locker-first scenes, the bridge-word change without its J++ part plus the pointer write mu_k - mu_j at s = 2 to each other slot k, against the write alone and against a random vector of the write's norm; the recall classified by the attribute it names; sealed"
question: Without the lens-readable identity (the change minus its J++ part), does a pointer write mu_k - mu_j at the bridge token make the recall name the item at the written slot k: does the recall dereference the same address the lookup uses and recall from the mention it lands on?
why_it_matters: The 9B's recall keeps ~45% of its switches with J++ removed at the bridge (locker-first), and the strong pointer write makes recalls name the item at the written slot (~80% on the Qwens, x8 recall stage). title: Batch 47.3 on the Muse L26 (the old 45h): a computed bridge. The routes test (C2) with the asked pick described ("Iris picked the one known for honey."), the change at the cue token; without J++ / U / U' refit on these scenes, each against a random part of its share; sealed
command: BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP= uv run python scripts/x47_cue.py run --name muse30_x47_cue
question: When the bridge must be recalled from a description ("the one known for honey"), does the lookup still go around the lens, and does it ever take the value?
why_it_matters: Every routes and main-test scene so far names the bridge. The lens's own rule says flexible computation routes through the J-space; a bridge the model must recall from a cue is where the lookup could need the lens part ((a'), the more interesting outcome) or keep going around it ((a)). "Never the value" and a pointer at the cue token (U') say whether the around route is the same one as for a named bridge.

decision_rule:
Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.3, verbatim): (a) "the split holds for a recalled bridge": gap >= 0.3 and lookup extra loss <= 0.10; (a') "a recalled bridge is handed through the lens": lookup extra loss >= 0.20 (then the lens's rule, "flexible computation routes through the J-space", holds here and not for stated bridges; report it as the more interesting outcome, not as a failure); (b) "never the value": value <= 0.05; (c) "a pointer at the cue token": U' removal cuts position answers >= 0.30 beyond random. Report Zach's M->P numbers beside (toy suite: 12 / -2 / 0). Gate 0.80 per reader; a model that fails the gate is "not tested". As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before it). Scenes: x6_routes' generator (animals, seed 2510, 700 scenes), its condition C2 only: three one-token items A, B, C, their locker sentences first, stated by name ("The locker of the frog is 5."), then three pick sentences; the asked person's pick is a description, "

picked the one known for ." (the two other picks name B and C). O: the asked pick is A's cue. S: B's cue, and B's and C's locker sentences trade places with B's digit -> e (not in O). Cues: one word per animal, the last word of the pick sentence, one token on the model's tokenizer. Third-person sound verbs ("croaks", "barks", "quacks", "hoots") are two or more tokens on both tokenizers (on the Qwens only hops / spins / trots / bites / climbs / talks / marches are one), so every cue sits in the frame "known for " and each animal takes the first one-token word of its ordered candidates (x47_cue.CUES; a sound or behaviour first where one is one token). Gate: O's read accuracy (X0's chat read, the top token after the digit's space) >= 0.80 for each reader over every generated scene, never lowered; eligible: both readers say and read O's and S's answers right; the first 300 in scene order. The change h_S - h_O at the cue token at L26, added on O. Arms: whole; without J++ (signed OMP, k = 25, over the letter-token J++ atoms at L) and without a random part of its share (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L); without U (Alf of results/x0_probe/muse30b_x0_probe_v4, not refit; read only, the run itself is named muse30_) and its random part; without U' (P_cf refit on these scenes: x7_pcf's centered rank-4 PCA of the cue token's S - O over pairs where A's locker sentence trades places with B's and with C's, every digit kept, built from a seeded half of the generated scenes (seed 0, by scene); tested on the chosen scenes of the other half) and its random part. title: Batch 47.5 on the 9B (L12): followed or needed? On the changed prompt, the bridge word's state without its projection on the change's 25 OMP atoms at L (and at L..L+3, per-layer lens), against a random subspace of the same share; main-test scenes, both readers
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_zero.py run --name qwen35_9b_x47_5 --why "Batch 47, test 47.5 (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml; Q47.5): on S, the bridge word's state without its projection on Δ's 25 OMP atoms at L12 and at L12..15, against a random subspace of the same share of ||h_S||^2; main-test scenes; sealed"
question: Does the recall follow the J++ part at one layer, or need it? Zeroing the 25 OMP atoms of the change on the changed prompt at L, against a random part of the same share: how much of S's answers does each reader keep?
why_it_matters: "Without the J++ part" is a conflict test (J++ says the old item, the rest says the new one). Whether the recall needs the part is Zach's zeroing. On Muse the two disagree at mid depth (our gap 0.85; his +6.7). Decides the headline's verb.

hypotheses.Q47.5: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q47.5, per model: 9B; 27B; Muse); not committed when this spec was written, so the job is sealed: per-item outputs only, no verdict; scripts/x47_zero.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed.

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.5), verbatim: "Followed, not needed at one layer" if the recall keeps >= 0.80 of its answers under the zeroing, within 0.10 of the random arm; "needed" if it loses >= 0.30 beyond random. The lookup reported beside. Whatever the result, the README's verb for the main test becomes "follows / reads" unless "needed" holds on all three. Design, verbatim: "On S (the changed prompt), at the bridge token at L: project out the 25 OMP atoms of Delta from h_S; the random subspace of the same share; also the same over L..L+3 with the per-layer lens (OMP per layer). Both readers. Measure: share of S's answers kept." As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the run): scenes = the main test (two people swap picks; d1_topics_v3, chat) with X0's read gate (0.80 per reader on O unedited, >= 150 eligible) and eligibility (both readers say and read O's and S's answers right), the first 200 eligible scenes in scene order. Δ_l = h_S - h_O at the bridge word and layer l; "the 25 OMP atoms of Δ" = X0's signed-OMP picks over the J++ lens's letter-token atoms at l (x0_parts.omp_atoms; their span holds X0's J++ k = 25 part of Δ). "Project out ... from h_S" = at the bridge word of S the state h becomes h - Q Q^T h, Q an orthonormal basis of the atoms' span, an edit on the state as it arrives. "The random subspace of the same share" = h minus its projection on the first k columns of X0's random basis (seed 888 + l), k per item so that those columns hold the same share of ||h_S||^2 as the atoms' span on S's clean state (statement_positions.random_subspace_part's rule). "Over L..L+3" = the same edit at L, L+1, L+2 and L+3 in one forward, each with its own lens, Δ_l and OMP; above L it acts on the state already edited below (the random arm likewise, k per layer from S's clean state). "Share of S's answers kept" = the share of the eligible scenes whose top token at X0's chat read of S (the prompt with a digit's space token appended) is S's answer's first token, per reader (S unedited keeps ~1 by eligibility; reported). "Keeps >= 0.80 of its answers under the zeroing, within 0.10 of the random arm" = kept(zeroed at L) >= 0.80 and |kept(zeroed at L) - kept(random at L)| <= 0.10; "loses >= 0.30 beyond random" = kept(random at L) - kept(zeroed at L) >= 0.30; otherwise "neither". The rule is read on the recall at L ("at one layer"); the lookup and L..L+3 get the same numbers and bars, descriptive. Q47.5's answer per model is the recall's label at L. "Needed holds on all three" = "needed" on the 9B, the 27B and Muse; a model whose gate fails is "not tested" and cannot hold it, so the verb is then "follows / reads". Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9 at the bars); cluster-bootstrap CIs over the bridge items (10,000 resamples, seed 0; paired for the differences) beside them. Reported beside: per layer the atoms' share of ||h_S||^2 and of ||Δ||^2, the random part's achieved share and k, the norms. Code: scripts/x47_zero.py verdict (label, batch_verb).

title: Batch 47.2 on Muse (L26): harder pointer scenes, is the order code ordinal, categorical (first vs rest) or slot-specific? Six-locker routes moves; the slot means fit on a held-out half; removals and writes on the other half (sealed)
command: export BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_six.py run --name muse30_x47_2 --why "batch 47, test 47.2 (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml; Q47.2): six-locker routes moves (the bridge's locker sentence moved from slot i to slot j, every ordered pair), the layout-free slot means fit on a held-out half, then on the other half the slot subspace and the old U removed against random parts, pairwise writes mu_t - mu_i, and the shift v = mean_k (mu_k+1 - mu_k) from every start slot; sealed"
question: In six-locker scenes, is the pointer's order code ordinal (a line over slots that one shift vector moves along), categorical (first locker vs the rest), or slot-specific (binding IDs: pairwise moves work, no common shift)?
why_it_matters: The pointer marks the first locker in a clean three-locker layout; the 2nd-vs-3rd removal found no separate direction, yet writing mu_3 - mu_2 moves the lookup at 2x. Three lockers cannot tell "first vs rest" from "a line over slots". Ordinal = a positional line the lens cannot read (Dai et al. 2024's ordering subspace); categorical = a one-bit marker; slot-specific = binding IDs (Feng & Steinhardt 2023).

hypotheses.Q47.2: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q47.2: ordinal / categorical, first vs rest / slot-specific, per model: 9B; Muse); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x47_six.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.2): "Ordinal": the first PCA component of the slot means is monotone in slot (|Spearman| >= 0.9) and v sends >= 0.25 of lookups to slot k+1 from >= 4 of 5 start slots, the random vector <= 0.05; "Categorical, first vs rest": v works only from slot 1 (others < 0.10) and U's removal on 2-6 moves is within 0.10 of random; "Slot-specific": pairwise writes reach >= 0.25 on most pairs but no single v does. Dumbest ways: (1) position share near 0 under the whole change -> "not interpretable" (the whole-change routes split reported first); (2) mu_2 - mu_1 reported separately and v fit without it; (3) letters A-H if digits run out. AS COMPUTED (written before any run; Dan may override before the run; scripts/x47_six.py docstring): SCENES: x6_routes' generator (its animal and people pools, sentences, encoding, chat rendering, X0's top-token read) with six single-token animals and their lockers (slots 1-6, six distinct digits of 1-9), the six locker sentences first, then three pick sentences (the asked person picks the bridge, two others pick two other locker items, order seeded), every item's first mention its locker sentence (checked per scene). A routes move (i, j) is x6_routes' C1 at six slots: the bridge's own locker sentence moves from slot i to slot j (swapped with the sentence at slot j; the bridge and the picks stay O's) and the bridge's number in S is a new digit not in O's list (7 of the 9 digits are used: no letters needed). Read on O: identity (= nothing) -> slot i's digit, position -> slot j's digit, value -> the new digit, other. 40 candidates per ordered pair (30 pairs; seed 4702, one stream per pair), the first 20 eligible per pair. C0 sanity (x6_routes' C0 at six slots: S = O with the asked person picking another person's item, the legs differ): 150 candidates, the first 100 eligible, whole change only; its lookup switch reported beside the three-locker reference (none for Muse: reported without one), descriptive: it does not stop the run. GATE: X0's competence (8 greedy tokens and the read, unedited O and S, both readers); O's read accuracy >= 0.80 per reader over the 1,200 move candidates; eligible = both readers say and read O's and S's answers right. If six slots miss the gate, the same at five slots (20 pairs x 40 candidates; 4-d slot subspace; (iv) on moves among slots 2-5; the ordinal count needs 4 of 4 start slots), decided by the competence step before any patch and recorded (manifest slots / fallback, gate.json); if five miss too: not tested. SPLIT: per ordered pair, the chosen scenes shuffled (seed 4721 keyed by the pair), the first half (floor) is the fit half, the rest the test half (stratified by pair, not by entity). FIT (in the job, on the fit half, before any arm): O's and S's states at the bridge word at L, each labelled by the bridge's slot in that prompt; x0_massmean's layout-free method (each state minus the mean of its layout group, x0_probe.layout, here the asked pick's place among the three picks; groups of one dropped); mu_k = slot k's mean; the slot subspace W = x0_massmean.mass_mean (orthonormal, rank 5). PCA of the six centred means: the variance explained by 1, 2, 3 components (cumulative), and the Spearman correlation of the first component's projection with slot (computed by the verdict from fit.npz). UNIT: the median over the test half of ||W W^T Delta|| (Delta = h_S - h_O at the bridge word); a write at dose s has norm s x unit. title: Batch 48, test 48.2 design A on the 9B (L12): does the recall's attribute (legs) get written at the bridge token after L, keyed by the change's J++ part? Legs probes at layers 12, 14, ..., 31 (entities held out), read under the main test's arms (whole / without J++ / without a random part); the last-token fallback in the same job
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x48_enrich.py run_a --name qwen35_9b_x48_2a --why "batch 48, test 48.2 design A (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml; Q48.2): legs probes at the bridge token (and the last token) at layers L, L+2, ..., last, entities held out, read under the main test's arms at L12; sealed"
question: After the bridge token's change at L, does a probe for the recall attribute (the item's number of legs), trained on unedited prompts with bridge entities held out, move from the original item's class to the changed item's at the later layers of the bridge token, and does that movement need the change's J++ part (25 OMP atoms) rather than a random part of the same share?
why_it_matters: The account under test (batch 48) says the recall is fact retrieval keyed on the lens-readable identity: MLPs at the bridge token enrich it with the item's attributes after L, which the last token reads out. If so, the attribute probe should follow the whole change and the no-random arm but not the no-J++ arm. If the probe does not read the attribute at the bridge token at all, the attribute is assembled at the last token instead, and the same test runs there (rule A's fallback, automatic in this job).

hypotheses.Q48.2: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q48.2 A); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x48_enrich.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml, 48.2 rule A): "J++ keys the enrichment" if at layers >= L+4 the probe moves >= 0.6 of the way under whole and under the random arm, and <= 0.3 under without-J++ (CI excluding the random arm's), on both models; if the probe does not read the attribute at the bridge token at all (held-out accuracy < 2x chance at every layer), run the same at the last token. As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the run): items = the main-test X0 run's 200 chat items at L12 (qwen35_9b_x0_necessity), rebuilt and checked against its ids; O = the original prompt, S = the changed one. Arms at L12 at the bridge token on O: whole = h_S - h_O; no_jpp = the change minus its J++ part (signed OMP, k = 25, the J++ lens atoms at L as X0 takes them); no_rand = minus a random part of the same share (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L). The probe: one per domain, one-hot ridge on standardized states (x0_probe's probe; penalty chosen by entity-held-out CV), trained on the unedited O prompts of every chat scene of the set (600; animals 200 scenes, 32 entities, classes 2 / 4 / 6 / 8), entities split into 5 folds (seed 0); held-out accuracy = out-of-fold accuracy; chance = 1 / the classes present. The rule's domain is animals (legs): elements and greek have one bridge entity per class (6 and 8 entities), so an entity-held-out probe never saw the held-out class and sits at 0 by construction; their probes and readings are written and reported as descriptive, outside the rule. States at the bridge token and at the last token (the recall's read position: the prompt with the digit's space token appended), at layers 12, 14, ..., 30 and 31. Reading an item: the probe trained on the folds that hold out both the original's and the changed item's entity; m(h) = score(changed item's class) - score(original item's class); the fraction of the way = (m(arm) - m(O)) / (m(S) - m(O)), clipped to [0, 1], over the items whose unedited gap m(S) - m(O) is positive (the rest counted, not read). Branch: the bridge token if the animals probe's held-out accuracy reaches 2x chance at some probed layer there, else the last token (recorded in probe.json). Holds on a model if at every probed layer >= L+4 where the probe reads the attribute (held-out >= 2x chance) the mean fraction is >= 0.6 under whole and under no_rand, <= 0.3 under no_jpp, and the paired cluster-bootstrap CI of no_rand - no_jpp (over the original bridge entities, 10,000, seed 0) excludes 0; on the batch if on both models. n for the rule: 68 animals items (26 entities). Scored by hand: scripts/x48_enrich.py verdict (EPS 1e-9 at the bars).

title: Batch 47 amendment 3, D1 + D2 on the 9B (L12): the token x layer causal map (S's state placed into O at one token group and one layer, every 2nd layer), with 47.4's cumulative arms as margins, and window patching (the bridge at every layer >= l); main test and clean design, both readers; SEALED until Q-depth
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_depthmap.py run --name qwen35_9b_x47_depthmap --why "batch 47, amendment 3 (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml; D1 + D2, Q-depth, sealed): the token x layer map and window patching on the main test's and the clean design's items at L12"
question: Where and when does each reader read the change: at which token group and which layer does placing S's state into O switch the answer? In locker-after scenes, does the lookup's mass sit at the locker sentences rather than the bridge word? In locker-first scenes, does the lookup's bridge-word mass end before the recall's, and does the recall have a second hot token at the item's earlier mention? After which layer is the bridge word no longer read (D2's l_R)?
why_it_matters: 47.4 asked why not every answer switches; D1 answers it as causal tracing for our two readers (the mass at other tokens and layers), and D2 gives one depth number per reader (the read-out layer) to set against Zach's late "question" band on the same model.

hypotheses.Q-depth: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q-depth: D1 (a), (b), (c) and D2 yes / no per model); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x47_depthmap.py verdict / view / figures refuse until it is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, D1 and D2). D1: (a) in locker-after scenes the lookup's mass sits at the locker sentences, not at the bridge word, at every layer (bridge-word cells <= 0.25 everywhere; some locker-sentence cell >= 0.5); (b) in locker-first scenes the lookup's bridge-word mass ends before the recall's (the last layer with bridge-word switch >= 0.3 is earlier for the lookup, by >= 2 layers on the 9B, >= 4 on Muse); (c) the recall's map has a second hot token, the item's earlier mention, in locker-first scenes (>= 0.3 at some layer), absent in locker-after. D2: "the handover from the mention to the question" if l_R(recall) lies at or below the start of Zach's late band on the 9B and 27B (9B L26-29, 27B L52-60). As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before the run): Items: x47_cumulative's (the main test's X0 run at L, qwen35_9b_x0_necessity, its 200 scenes, the mixed ones in "all" only; the 45m clean-design run qwen35_9b_x45m_fresh, its locker-first and locker-after scenes, its 100 mixed scenes left out for the budget), with x47_cumulative's asserts (O and S the same length, changed only at the bridge (clean) or the bridge and one token of the other person's pick (main); the asked pick sentence at the same positions with the same ids but the bridge's; the readers' prompts equal through the last patched context token). Order groups: x45m's (locker-first = the bridge's and S's bridge's locker sentences both before the asked pick; locker-after = both after). Both readers; their prompts differ from the question on, so S's states are taken per reader (one unedited forward of S and of O per reader and item, the read's space token appended). Layers: 0, 2, ..., 30 (every 2nd; the last block's output is read by nothing). Cells: S's block-l output set (exp04's SetRows, not added) into O at one token group, O's own tokens; token groups by character overlap in the rendered prompt: bridge (the bridge word); pick_rest (the asked pick sentence without the bridge and the person); person (the asked person's token); per locker sentence its item token(s) and its number token(s), the sentences named by role (lk_org = O's bridge's, lk_cf = S's bridge's: the added one in the clean design, the other person's original pick's in the main test; lk_other1, lk_other2 = the rest in context order); question (from the question's first token to the end of the prompt, the template's closing tokens and 'Answer:' included); last (the read position, the appended space token). The bridge is the only group whose token id differs between O and S; its row has one more cell, emb = O's prompt with S's token at the bridge and no state placed (the input embedding; block 0's input as a layer). Every other group's tokens are identical in O and S, and S's state there still differs downstream of the bridge: a cell measures what those tokens have read. In the main test the other person's changed pick is in no group; S's states at every group after it carry it too (it is what 47.4's (d)->100% measured), and in main items where that pick comes first the b margin and the bridge cells differ from the clean design's by it. Margins: b<l> = the bridge swapped at every layer <= l (blocks 0..l and its input embedding), one per sampled l; d = the whole asked pick sentence swapped at every layer (and the bridge's embedding). D2: w<l> = S's state set at the bridge at every block output >= l (O's tokens; the complement of b), one per sampled l; l_R per reader = the first sampled l at which the w curve is <= 0.1 (none: not reached). Beside them: none (O unedited), a (47.4's (a): h_S - h_O added at the bridge at L; X0's whole arm) and S read on S. Cell value = the switch rate over the order group's items (X0's chat read; switch = the top token is S's answer's first token), 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals over bridge items (10,000, seed 0, every arm on the same draws). question: At the bridge word at L12, is there a low-dimensional subspace of the change that mediates the lookup, one that mediates the recall, are they disjoint (own-IIA high, cross-IIA low), and where do they sit against the lens (J++-25), the pointer directions U and the input-embedding part W_E-25?
why_it_matters: We know what the lookup's identity code is not (not J++ at K = 25, not W_E at K = 100, not the layer's main directions). A learned subspace that mediates the lookup, measured against the lens, U and W_E, says what it is, with how many dimensions, and whether it is disjoint from the recall's.

hypotheses.Q48.1: Dan's answers in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q48.1, one option and a confidence per letter (a)-(d)); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x48_das.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml, 48.1): (a) two readers, two subspaces: own-IIA >= 0.7 at some k <= 16 for both readers and cross-IIA <= 0.25 in both directions (paired CI excluding overlap with own-IIA); (b) the recall's subspace is the lens's part: R_recall's energy inside J++-25 >= 0.5 (random R <= 0.15), R_lookup's <= 0.2; (c) the address is part of the lookup's subspace: ||R_lookup^T U||_F^2 / 4 >= 0.5 (random R ~ k/d); (d) a third identity code: R_lookup's energy outside (J++-25 u U u W_E-25) >= 0.5 while its own-IIA >= 0.7, and R_lookup alone gives identity answers >= 0.3 in the routes read. Fallback: if own-IIA stays < 0.5 at k = 64 for the lookup, "no low-dimensional mediator at this token and layer". As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override): pairs = the stored main-test run's (qwen35_9b_x0_necessity, chat, L12) eligible scenes that are locker-first (both items' locker sentences before the asked pick, x0_strata) and that the stored whole change switches for at least one reader; each reader trains and is read on the pairs the whole change switches for it (lookup 72, recall 75 of 75; the scene ids in pairs.json). Split by the original bridge entity 60 / 20 / 20 (train / select k / test), seed 0 (32 entities: 19 / 6 / 7; lookup pairs 44 / 10 / 18, recall 46 / 10 / 19). Intervention h <- h_O + R R^T (h_S - h_O) at the bridge token at L12 on the O prompt, R [d x k] with orthonormal columns (torch.nn.utils.parametrizations.orthogonal); loss = cross-entropy of S's answer's first token at X0's chat read position (the appended space); Adam lr 1e-3, 300 steps, batch 16 (micro-batches of 8, gradient accumulation); h_O / h_S cached once per pair, the training forwards real (the layers after L12 are needed for the loss), the IIA evaluated with X0's read (generate_batch, the AddRows edit). Chosen k per reader = the smallest k <= 16 whose select-split own-IIA >= 0.7, else the k with the highest select own-IIA; every rule read at the chosen k on the test entities' pairs: point estimates = means over the reader's test pairs, cluster-bootstrap CIs over bridge entities (10,000, seed 0) beside them. "Paired CI excluding overlap with own-IIA" = the paired bootstrap of own-IIA minus cross-IIA over the reader's test pairs has a lower bound > 0; cross-IIA for a reader = its switch rate under the other reader's R at that reader's chosen k. Energy inside a part = the share of ||R R^T Delta||^2 in the span of the pair's 25 signed-OMP J++ atoms (J++-25; also 100), of its 25 W_E atoms (x0_necessity's "we" dictionary), or of U (x0_massmean.subspaces' Alf on qwen35_9b_x0_probe_v4, rank 4); outside = 1 minus the share in the orthonormalised union of the three; cos^2 with U = ||R^T U||_F^2 / rank(U) (x6_routes.mean_cos2; a random R: k / d). The routes read: R_lookup alone (at the chosen k) written on the first 100 eligible x6_routes C2 scenes (another item moved); identity answers = the lookup's top token is the new item's own locker digit. IIA divided by the whole change's rerun switch rate on the test pairs reported beside. Energy >= 0.8 of Delta flags the R "not selective". Scored by hand: scripts/x48_das.py verdict (EPS 1e-9 at the bars).

the whole change and O unedited reread on the select and test pairs (the ceiling and the floor; IIA / S_whole reported)
cross-IIA: R_lookup read by the recall, R_recall read by the lookup (the disjointness clause of (a))
the read position: both readers' prompts identical through the bridge token (asserted per pair), each read at its own last token (the appended space); the index per reader recorded in cases.jsonl

title: Batch 48.1 on Muse (L26): DAS at the bridge word, two readers, two subspaces? R_lookup and R_recall (k = 1, 4, 16, 64) trained on the main test's locker-first pairs; own-IIA, cross-IIA, energy inside J++-25 / U / W_E-25, routes read; random and shuffled-target baselines
command: export BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x48_das.py run --name muse30_x48_das --why "batch 48, test 48.1 (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml; Q48.1): DAS at the bridge word at L26 on the main test's locker-first pairs the whole change switches; one R per reader and k, random and shuffled-target baselines; sealed"
question: At the bridge word at L26, is there a low-dimensional subspace of the change that mediates the lookup, one that mediates the recall, are they disjoint (own-IIA high, cross-IIA low), and where do they sit against the lens (J++-25), the pointer directions U and the input-embedding part W_E-25?
why_it_matters: We know what the lookup's identity code is not (not J++ at K = 25, not W_E at K = 100, not the layer's main directions). A learned subspace that mediates the lookup, measured against the lens, U and W_E, says what it is, with how many dimensions, and whether it is disjoint from the recall's; Muse is the second model the rule needs.

hypotheses.Q48.1: Dan's answers in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q48.1, one option and a confidence per letter (a)-(d), for Muse); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x48_das.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml, 48.1): (a) two readers, two subspaces: own-IIA >= 0.7 at some k <= 16 for both readers and cross-IIA <= 0.25 in both directions (paired CI excluding overlap with own-IIA); (b) the recall's subspace is the lens's part: R_recall's energy inside J++-25 >= 0.5 (random R <= 0.15), R_lookup's <= 0.2; (c) the address is part of the lookup's subspace: ||R_lookup^T U||_F^2 / 4 >= 0.5 (random R ~ k/d); (d) a third identity code: R_lookup's energy outside (J++-25 u U u W_E-25) >= 0.5 while its own-IIA >= 0.7, and R_lookup alone gives identity answers >= 0.3 in the routes read. Fallback: if own-IIA stays < 0.5 at k = 64 for the lookup, "no low-dimensional mediator at this token and layer". As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override): pairs = the stored main-test run's (muse30b_x0_necessity, chat, L26) eligible scenes that are locker-first (both items' locker sentences before the asked pick, x0_strata) and that the stored whole change switches for at least one reader; each reader trains and is read on the pairs the whole change switches for it (lookup 55, recall 31 of 58; the scene ids in pairs.json). Split by the original bridge entity 60 / 20 / 20 (train / select k / test), seed 0 (28 entities: 17 / 6 / 5; lookup pairs 32 / 15 / 8, recall 15 / 11 / 5). Intervention h <- h_O + R R^T (h_S - h_O) at the bridge token at L26 on the O prompt, R [d x k] with orthonormal columns (torch.nn.utils.parametrizations.orthogonal); loss = cross-entropy of S's answer's first token at X0's chat read position (the appended space); Adam lr 1e-3, 300 steps, batch 16 (micro-batches of 8, gradient accumulation); h_O / h_S cached once per pair, the training forwards real (the layers after L26 are needed for the loss), the IIA evaluated with X0's read (generate_batch, the AddRows edit). Chosen k per reader = the smallest k <= 16 whose select-split own-IIA >= 0.7, else the k with the highest select own-IIA; every rule read at the chosen k on the test entities' pairs: point estimates = means over the reader's test pairs, cluster-bootstrap CIs over bridge entities (10,000, seed 0) beside them. "Paired CI excluding overlap with own-IIA" = the paired bootstrap of own-IIA minus cross-IIA over the reader's test pairs has a lower bound > 0; cross-IIA for a reader = its switch rate under the other reader's R at that reader's chosen k. Energy inside a part = the share of ||R R^T Delta||^2 in the span of the pair's 25 signed-OMP J++ atoms (J++-25; also 100), of its 25 W_E atoms (x0_necessity's "we" dictionary), or of U (x0_massmean.subspaces' Alf on muse30b_x0_probe_v4, rank 4); outside = 1 minus the share in the orthonormalised union of the three; cos^2 with U = ||R^T U||_F^2 / rank(U) (x6_routes.mean_cos2; a random R: k / d). The routes read: R_lookup alone (at the chosen k) written on the first 100 eligible x6_routes C2 scenes (another item moved); identity answers = the lookup's top token is the new item's own locker digit. IIA divided by the whole change's rerun switch rate on the test pairs reported beside. Energy >= 0.8 of Delta flags the R "not selective". Scored by hand: scripts/x48_das.py verdict (EPS 1e-9 at the bars).

title: Batch 48, test 48.2 design A on the Muse (L26): does the recall's attribute (legs) get written at the bridge token after L, keyed by the change's J++ part? Legs probes at layers 26, 28, ..., 51 (entities held out), read under the main test's arms (whole / without J++ / without a random part); the last-token fallback in the same job
command: export BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x48_enrich.py run_a --name muse30_x48_2a --why "batch 48, test 48.2 design A (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml; Q48.2): legs probes at the bridge token (and the last token) at layers L, L+2, ..., last, entities held out, read under the main test's arms at L26; sealed"
question: After the bridge token's change at L, does a probe for the recall attribute (the item's number of legs), trained on unedited prompts with bridge entities held out, move from the original item's class to the changed item's at the later layers of the bridge token, and does that movement need the change's J++ part (25 OMP atoms) rather than a random part of the same share?
why_it_matters: The account under test (batch 48) says the recall is fact retrieval keyed on the lens-readable identity: MLPs at the bridge token enrich it with the item's attributes after L, which the last token reads out. If so, the attribute probe should follow the whole change and the no-random arm but not the no-J++ arm. If the probe does not read the attribute at the bridge token at all, the attribute is assembled at the last token instead, and the same test runs there (rule A's fallback, automatic in this job).

hypotheses.Q48.2: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q48.2 A); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x48_enrich.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml, 48.2 rule A): "J++ keys the enrichment" if at layers >= L+4 the probe moves >= 0.6 of the way under whole and under the random arm, and <= 0.3 under without-J++ (CI excluding the random arm's), on both models; if the probe does not read the attribute at the bridge token at all (held-out accuracy < 2x chance at every layer), run the same at the last token. As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the run): items = the main-test X0 run's 200 chat items at L26 (muse30b_x0_necessity), rebuilt and checked against its ids; O = the original prompt, S = the changed one. Arms at L26 at the bridge token on O: whole = h_S - h_O; no_jpp = the change minus its J++ part (signed OMP, k = 25, the J++ lens atoms at L as X0 takes them); no_rand = minus a random part of the same share (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L). The probe: one per domain, one-hot ridge on standardized states (x0_probe's probe; penalty chosen by entity-held-out CV), trained on the unedited O prompts of every chat scene of the set (530 on the Muse's tokenizer; animals 176 scenes, 31 entities, classes 2 / 4 / 6 / 8), entities split into 5 folds (seed 0); held-out accuracy = out-of-fold accuracy; chance = 1 / the classes present. The rule's domain is animals (legs): elements and greek have one bridge entity per class (6 and 7 entities), so an entity-held-out probe never saw the held-out class and sits at 0 by construction; their probes and readings are written and reported as descriptive, outside the rule. States at the bridge token and at the last token (the recall's read position: the prompt with the digit's space token appended), at layers 26, 28, ..., 50 and 51. Reading an item: the probe trained on the folds that hold out both the original's and the changed item's entity; m(h) = score(changed item's class) - score(original item's class); the fraction of the way = (m(arm) - m(O)) / (m(S) - m(O)), clipped to [0, 1], over the items whose unedited gap m(S) - m(O) is positive (the rest counted, not read). Branch: the bridge token if the animals probe's held-out accuracy reaches 2x chance at some probed layer there, else the last token (recorded in probe.json). Holds on a model if at every probed layer >= L+4 where the probe reads the attribute (held-out >= 2x chance) the mean fraction is >= 0.6 under whole and under no_rand, <= 0.3 under no_jpp, and the paired cluster-bootstrap CI of no_rand - no_jpp (over the original bridge entities, 10,000, seed 0) excludes 0; on the batch if on both models. n for the rule: 68 animals items (27 entities). Scored by hand: scripts/x48_enrich.py verdict (EPS 1e-9 at the bars).
controls: no_rand: the change minus a random part of the J++ part's share (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L): the dose-matched control the no_jpp arm must undercut
the unedited gap: O and S unedited define 0 and 1 of the fraction; items the probe does not separate on the unedited states are counted and not read
entities held out (5 folds, seed 0): the probe reads an attribute feature, not identity; the reading probe also holds the changed item's entity out
both readers' reads under every arm beside the states, and the rerun whole / no_jpp switches against the main run's stored ones (descriptive check)
the last token probed in the same job: rule A's fallback, taken automatically when the bridge token's probe is under 2x chance at every layer

title: Batch 47.6 (b) on the 9B (L12): is the pointer formed by the pick token reading the locker sentences before L? Exact edge knock-outs on the routes scenes with a filler sentence, full-attention-only and all-layer (DeltaNet) blocks beside each other; part (c) dropped (Dan, amendment 1); SEALED until Q47.6
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_edges.py run --part b --name qwen35_9b_x47_6_b --why "batch 47, test 47.6 b (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml; Q47.6, sealed; part c dropped by Dan's amendment 1): formation, the change formed with the asked pick sentence blind to the locker sentences at 0..L, against the same number of edges to a filler sentence"
question: Is the pointer formed by the pick token reading the locker sentences before L: if the asked pick sentence cannot read the locker sentences at layers 0..L while the change is formed, do the lookup's position answers vanish while its identity answers and the recall's switch stay?
why_it_matters: The routes test says the lookup follows a position code (the pointer, U) that the lens cannot read (0.51 of the 9B's C2 lookups under the whole change). Formation at the pick token from the locker sentences before L would place the first step of the around route, not through the lens. Exact knock-outs block only the named reads (DeltaNet included), so a fall is not a size effect of a residual edit. Part (c), the dereference block, was dropped by Dan (amendment 1, ~02:30): blocking the question's reads of the locker sentences kills the lookup under every hypothesis.

hypotheses.Q47.6: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q47.6, formation only); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x47_edges.py verdict / view / figures refuse until it is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.6 b; (c) dropped by Dan's amendment 1, batch48.yaml): "the pointer is formed by the pick token reading the lockers" if position answers fall to <= 0.10 (from 0.51 / 0.54) while identity answers stay within 0.10 and the recall's switch within 0.10, on Muse and the 9B; the control within 0.10 of none. As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before the run): Scenes: the routes test's C2 scenes (x6_routes.scenes, seed 2510, locker-first) with one neutral filler sentence first in O and in S, identical ("A light rain began to fall just after the doors were closed, and the old radio in the corner played softly through the whole day.": 27 tokens on this tokenizer, the three locker sentences' total, checked per item); x6_routes.encode keeps the bridge one token at one index shared by O and S (plan, 28 Oct: 700 of 700 scenes kept). Gate: O's read accuracy >= 0.80 per reader on these prompts, else the model is "not tested" (never a lowered gate); eligible: both readers say and read O's and S's answers right; the first 300 in scene order. Edges are (block, source token, destination token) with every source before every destination; DeltaNet blocks in knockout's "value" mode (the source's values and conv taps in the value channels removed, every weight kept), full-attention blocks with the pair's logits at -inf in every head; indirect routes stay open. The change Delta = h_S - h_O at the bridge word (block L's output) is formed with the block active in both forwards that form it, O's and S's (the asked pick sentence's 5 tokens cannot read the locker sentences' 27 tokens at blocks 0..L, L included); that Delta is added at the bridge word at L on O, which is read unblocked, as in the routes test; none = Delta formed without a block (same batch). The decisive arms are block/sentence/all (13 blocks, 1755 edges: 405 in full-attention blocks 3, 7, 11, 1350 in DeltaNet blocks) and its control/sentence/all (the filler's 27 tokens as sources, the same destinations and blocks: 1755 edges). Position / identity share = the share of the 300 items whose lookup answer x6_routes.classify calls position / identity; recall switch = the recall's top token is S's answer. Holds on the 9B iff position(block) <= 0.10, |identity(block) - identity(none)| <= 0.10, |recall(block) - recall(none)| <= 0.10, and the control within 0.10 of none on each of the three (two-sided: a rise counts). Beside it, not in the rule: dests = the bridge token alone (dumbest way 2: 351 edges), and the full-attention-only blocks (405 / 81 edges), each with its matched control. The period of the pick sentence comes after the bridge, so it cannot reach the bridge's state at L; "sentence" differs from "bridge" by the person token, "picked" and "the". No (c) arm runs (the --with-c flag is off). The test holds iff it holds on Muse and on the 9B. Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9 at the bars); 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals over the bridge items (10,000, seed 0) beside them. Scored by hand after Q47.6 is committed: scripts/x47_edges.py verdict.
controls: control/<dests>/<layers>: exactly as many edges, from the filler sentence's 27 tokens instead of the locker sentences' 27 (same destinations, same blocks; asserted per item)
none: the change formed without a block, in the same batch as the blocked ones; unedited O read beside
the recall's switch: the check that the block does not break identity (dumbest way 1)
dests = the bridge token alone (dumbest way 2) and full-attention-only blocks (9B), each with its matched control
