title: Batch 47.7(a) on the 27B (L32): question-first routes scenes, does the model prefetch the number at the bridge word, and is a prefetched value in the J-space? Routes shares, the value probe and the lens's digit rank, question-first vs question-last; arms whole / without J++ (digits allowed) / random / without U / random
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.6-27b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_value.py run --part a --name x47_7a_27b --why "batch 47, test 47.7(a) (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml; Q47.7): the routes scenes with each reader's question before the context; routes shares under every arm question-first, the whole change question-last beside it, the lookup's O state at the bridge word in both renderings for the value probe and the lens's digit rank; sealed"
question: When the question comes before the context in the same user turn, does the lookup's answer under the whole change ever follow the locker value (the number of the moved item's new locker sentence), does a linear probe read the answer digit at the bridge word where it could not with the question last, and if a value route appears, is it carried by the J++ part and visible to the lens?
why_it_matters: The routes test says the lookup keeps an address at the bridge word, never the number, when the question comes last (value 0 of 300 on four models). If the model prefetches the number once it knows the question, 'never the value' is a fact about question order, not about the representation; and whether a prefetched value lives in the J-space tests the workspace account's 'surfaced to the J-space on demand'. 'Address regardless' is the stronger version of 'never the value'.

hypotheses.Q47.7: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q47.7); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x47_value.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule:
Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.7, amendment 1). As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the enqueue): the layer fixed in advance (32); the change h_S - h_O at the bridge word; arms whole, without the J++ part (signed OMP, k = 25, over the lens atoms of the letter tokens AND the digit tokens: the main test's letter-only restriction is lifted here), without a random part of its share (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + layer), without U (x0_massmean's Alf of the x0_probe_v4 states, not refit), without a random part of its share; the lookup's answer classified identity / position / value / original / other by the top token at the read step; route shares with cluster-bootstrap intervals over bridge items (10,000, seed 0); a value at a bar counts as at the bar (EPS 1e-9). Sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x47_value.py verdict refuses until Dan's Q47.7 is committed). Question-first prompt: the user turn is 'Question: <q> <the digit instruction>

<context>', the chat template, the assistant turn prefilled 'Answer:' (question-last: x6_routes' prompt, '<context>
<q> <instruction>'; the instruction block moves with the question). With the question first the two readers' prompts differ before the bridge, so the change is computed per reader from its own prompts (question-last: one change from the lookup's prompt, read by both). The bridge is asserted the same token at the same offset from the context's first token in both renderings, one token at one index in O and S (0 of 1,400 dropped on this tokenizer; its absolute index moves by the question block, 20 / 21 tokens on Qwen, 19 / 20 on Muse). Digits vs slots: a permutation chi-square test on the generated set, asserted p >= 0.01 (this tokenizer's set: O p = 0.29, S p = 0.58). Gate 0.80 per reader and condition on the question-first prompts (below it: not tested); eligible = both readers say and read O and S right in both renderings (the question-last competence rows are the x6_routes run's, its prompts being these exactly, asserted); the first 300 per condition. Value probe: x0_probe's ridge probe for the answer digit at the lookup's O state at the bridge word, 5 folds with whole entities held out, one state per O context, question-first vs question-last. Lens: the rank of the answer digit among the 10 digit tokens under the lens's vectors at that state (X0's digit check), the share ranked first. Rule per model: prefetch on demand if the question-first C2 value share >= 0.15 and the probe >= 0.6 (the premise, question-last value <= 0.05 and probe <= 0.4, checked and reported); the prefetched value is in the J-space (read only where prefetch holds) if without J++ the value share falls >= 0.3 beyond the random part and the lens ranks the digit first in >= 0.4 of items; address regardless if the value share <= 0.05 and the probe within 0.1 of question-last. Over the models: a label holds on >= 2 of 3. Beside it: the position share question-first minus question-last (the whole change, paired) with its interval. C0 (the sanity swap) question-first against x6_routes' reference (within 0.10; Muse >= 0.5): written to c0_check.json, the run does not stop; a failed model is labelled 'C0 failed' at the verdict.
controls: a random part at the J++ part's share and at U's share of the change, per item
the whole change question-last in the same run (the paired position / value difference) and the x6_routes runs (value 0 of 300)
the recall reader on its own question-first patch
the value probe question-last at the same layer on the same scenes (x0_probe v4: 9B / 27B at chance, Muse 0.33), and the lens rank question-last (8% / 13% first on the 9B / 27B)
C0 (the sanity swap) question-first against the question-last reference
n: 700 scenes per condition generated (C0, C2; seed 2510, x6_routes' scenes), 0 dropped at the question-first encoding, the first 300 eligible per condition
notes: Batch 47 amendment 1 (Dan 28 Oct ~02:30), queue slot after 48.1 (9B); not cut. Estimate from the ledger: x6_routes_r2 (the 27B, 3 conditions: competence 2,100 cases x 2 readers, 900 items x (2 forwards + 2 reads of 6 rows)) 0.68 h; x45a_27b (1,500 items, 3,500-case competence) 1.05 h, x45a_9b 0.72 h, x45a_muse 0.74 h. Here: competence on 1,400 question-first cases x 2 readers (the question-last rows are reused from the x6_routes run), 600 items x (6 forwards: lookup and recall question-first O and S, lookup question-last O and S; 2 reads of 6 rows question-first, 2 reads of 2 rows question-last), one batched signed OMP. Roughly 1.1-1.2x the routes job per model: 9B 0.5, 27B 0.8, Muse 0.6 GPU-h (Dan's figure for (a): ~1.2 in total; the arithmetic says ~1.9). Writes manifest, plan (drops, the independence test, the bridge shift), cases, competence, gate, outcomes, norms, readout (lens ranks), states.npz + items (the probe's states), examples_greedy, c0_check; no verdict. By hand after Dan's Q47.7: uv run python scripts/x47_value.py verdict --part a --runs qwen35_9b_x47_7a x47_7a_27b muse30_x47_7a (CPU; writes the verdict and the verify-pack examples, 10 items seed 0).

title: Batch 47.7(c) on the 9B (L12): never the value, in prose / JSON / table? Varied scenes, locker-first, another item moved with a new number; identity / position / value shares, and without the per-format refit pointer from 45d vs random
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_value.py run --part c --name qwen35_9b_x47_7c --why "batch 47, test 47.7(c) (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml; Q47.7): the varied scenes (x0b_v2, prose / JSON / table), locker-first, the asked pick changed to another item whose locker statement trades places with a third item's and takes a new number; the lookup's route shares per format under the whole change and without J++ / U / the refit pointer vs random parts; sealed"
question: In the varied scenes (prose, JSON, tables), when the asked pick becomes another item whose locker statement moved and took a new number, does the lookup's answer under the whole change at the bridge word ever follow the value, and in JSON / table formats does it follow the position, carried by the per-format refit pointer?

"Reported late, not surfaced": the lens stays <= 0.1 at the bridge word under the report prompt and the report loses <= 0.1 without J++ but >= 0.3 without U; the address is converted to a word at the question, not at the token. A model that cannot report positions (gate < 0.80 on the report) is "not tested". As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before the run): Scenes: the routes generator's C0 scenes (x6_routes.scenes, seed 2510: three one-token animals, their three locker sentences first, then three picks; O: the asked person picked A, S: picked B, same lockers and digits; the asked item's locker in slot 1, 2 or 3 at random, the control of dumbest way 1), 500 generated, the first 200 eligible kept per order. Readers, four separate prompts over the same context (dumbest way 3; asserted: in the question-last order the four prompts share every token through the bridge word, and each reader's gate is computed on its own prompt): lookup "Which locker belongs to

's pick?" (digit), recall "How many legs does

's pick have?" (digit), report "Was the locker of

Two question orders, each with its own gate, items, change and reads: question-last (the question after the context, as every routes test) and question-first (the question and its instruction before the context, one user turn). Why both: in the question-last order the bridge word precedes the question, so its state at L is one and the same under the four prompts (causal attention; asserted on the ids) and the lens clause "under the report prompt vs the lookup prompt" cannot differ there; the question-first order is where surfacing on demand can show at the bridge word. (a) Handoff: l_P >= l_J, report l_P - l_J (Q35.1's failure on the 27B predicts a gap of about 4 layers there). (b) The address forms before it is used: l_probe <= l_P on every model; if the probe reaches 0.80 only after l_P, say so. (c) Identity leaves the lens: identity share with only-J++ >= 0.5 at the earliest interpretable layer and <= 0.1 by L, while identity with only-I_l rises to >= 0.3 by L, on >= 2 of 3 models; report the crossing layer. (d) Never the value, at any depth: value <= 0.05 at every interpretable layer. (e) The recall side: the layer window where the whole change switches the recall >= 0.5, and whether without-J++ costs it >= 0.3 throughout that window (the recall's own onset layer reported beside l_J). 'Not interpretable' where the whole change switches < 30% of a reader. As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before the run): Scenes: x6_routes' generator (seed 2510; locker-first), conditions C2 and C0, X0's gate (0.80 per reader on unedited scenes) and eligibility; the eligible C2 scenes split by bridge entity (seed 0; entities in a seeded order fill the test half to N_TEST scenes, the rest form the fit half, >= 150 or the run stops). Per sweep layer, from one forward of O and of S per scene: on the fit half the layout-free slot means and U_l (mass-mean basis; rank 2 with three lockers, the spec's rank 4 is not reachable here), the entity means over O and S bridge-word states and Id_l, x0_probe's three probes (entities held out), the refit's held-out slot / entity accuracy on the test half, the lens's top-10 rate for the bridge token; on the test half Delta = h_S - h_O and its parts J (signed OMP, 25 atoms of the layer's J++ lens, letter tokens), U (projection on U_l), I (rank-1 along mu_S - mu_O orthogonalised against the scene's atoms; zero where an entity has no mean, the scene left out of the I cells), W_E's 25-atom part and its overlap with J (D4). Random parts of the same share per scene: random lens atoms (seed 777 + l) for J, X0's random subspace (seed 888 + l) for U and I. Arms: none, whole, keep_X, keep_X_rand, no_X, no_X_rand for X in J, U, I; C0 scenes none and whole. Reads: X0's chat read, both readers; lookup answers classified identity / position / value / original / other, recall answers changed / original / slot item / other. Verdict (CPU, after Q47.8): per model and layer, shares and extra losses (X.cell) with cluster-bootstrap CIs over bridge entities (10,000, seed 0); the lookup's switch = identity + position + value, the recall's = changed; not interpretable where the whole change switches < 0.30; l_J, l_P, l_probe and rules (a)-(e) as the spec words them, point estimates, EPS 1e-9. controls: every keep-only and without arm paired with a random part of the same share of the change per scene: random lens atoms (seed 777 + layer) for the J++ part, X0's random subspace (seed 888 + layer) for U_l and I_l; the achieved random shares recorded per scene (norms.jsonl)

the sanity swap C0 (Iris picks the other item, nothing moves) read under the whole change at every layer; at L its lookup switch rate must be within 0.10 of the one-pick reference (Muse: >= 0.5), else the job fails after writing its files

the fit half and the test half share no bridge entity (split.json); the refits' held-out slot / entity accuracy on the test half and the lens's top-10 rate per layer are reported beside the arms (dumbest ways 1 and 3)
none (O unedited) read beside every arm; layers where the whole change switches < 30% of a reader are shaded and not read (dumbest way 2)
the recall reader on the same scenes and arms: changed item / original item / the item at the target slot / other
n: 200 test scenes (C2, another item moved) and their C0 base scenes; the fit half every other eligible C2 scene up to 250 (at least 150, else the run stops); plan on the 9B tokenizer (28 Oct): 700 C2 scenes generated, 32 bridge entities (10 to the test half, 22 to the fit half when all are eligible); x6_routes' eligibility on the 9B was 573 of 700

From results/jobq/ledger_sesterce-h100x2.jsonl (H100 PCIe) on the 9B: x6_routes_bothoff (600 C0+C2 cases, 2 forwards + 2 reads of 8 rows each) 1345 s against x6_routes_bothoff_ctrl (300 cases, 9 rows) 713 s gives ~1.05 s per case for 2 forwards + 2 small read calls, i.e. ~0.26 s per forward or small call, and ~400 s for the competence stage of 1,400 generated cases; a 128-row read call taken as 1 s. title:
Batch 47.10 on Muse (L26): report the address. Routes C0 scenes with a third reader, the report ('Was the locker of

's pick listed first, second or third?'; the digit variant beside), question-last and question-first; the lens's rank of the ordinal at the bridge word, the slot probe; the change at L whole / without J++ (letter and digit atoms) / without random / without U / without random / only U / only random; SEALED until Q47.10
command: export BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_report.py run --name muse30_x47_report --why "batch 47, amendment 4, test 47.10 (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml; Q47.10, sealed): the report reader on routes C0 scenes at L26, question-last and question-first; the lens's ordinal rank at the bridge word, the slot probe's states, and the arms"
question: Gurnee et al.: information not normally in the J-space can be surfaced to it on demand. The address (the pointer U) is not verbalizable (47.0). Does it become lens-readable, and lens-dependent, when the task is to report it: does the lens rank the correct ordinal at the bridge word under the report prompt, and does the report lose its switches without the J++ part (surfaced on demand), or does the report ignore J++ and need U (reported late, converted to a word at the question)?
why_it_matters: The routes tests found a lookup route around the lens (a pointer U the lens cannot read). If a reader whose task is to say the address pulls it into the J-space at the token, the J-space is where the model surfaces what it needs to verbalize (the workspace reading); if the report reads the same pointer around the lens and converts it to a word only at the question, the address stays outside the J-space even when it must be spoken: the same address, two consumers. Muse is the model where the lookup's loss without J++ was largest among the three (the Muse disagreement with Zach's zeroing), so its report is the sharpest test of "lens-dependent on demand".

hypotheses.Q47.10: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q47.10); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x47_report.py verdict / view / figures refuse until it is committed).

decision_rule:
Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.10): "Surfaced on demand": under the report prompt the lens ranks the correct ordinal in its top-5 in >= 0.4 of items (under the lookup prompt <= 0.1), and the report loses >= 0.3 of its switches without J++ beyond random, while the lookup on the same scenes loses <= 0.10 (as before). "Reported late, not surfaced": the lens stays <= 0.1 at the bridge word under the report prompt and the report loses <= 0.1 without J++ but >= 0.3 without U; the address is converted to a word at the question, not at the token. As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before the run): Scenes: the routes generator's C0 scenes (x6_routes.scenes, seed 2510: three one-token animals, their three locker sentences first, then three picks; O: the asked person picked A, S: picked B, same lockers and digits; the asked item's locker in slot 1, 2 or 3 at random, the control of dumbest way 1), 500 generated, the first 200 eligible kept per order. Readers, four separate prompts over the same context (dumbest way 3; asserted: in the question-last order the four prompts share every token through the bridge word, and each reader's gate is computed on its own prompt): lookup "Which locker belongs to

's pick?" (digit), recall "How many legs does

's pick have?" (digit), report "Was the locker of

's pick listed first, second or third?" (word; O's answer is A's slot's ordinal, S's is B's), report_digit "Was the locker of

's pick listed 1, 2 or 3?" (digit; beside: it neither gates nor selects items). Read: X0's chat read (tasks_v2's prompt, thinking off, 'Answer:' prefilled; Muse's template puts 'Answer:' right after the assistant header): a digit reader with the space token appended, the word reader right after 'Answer:' with its answer token ' first' / ' second' / ' third' (one token in all four spellings on this tokenizer: plan, 28 Oct); switch = the top token over the vocabulary is S's answer; right = O's. Two question orders, each with its own gate, items, change and reads: question-last (the question after the context, as every routes test) and question-first (the question and its instruction before the context, one user turn). Why both: in the question-last order the bridge word precedes the question, so its state at L is one and the same under the four prompts (causal attention; asserted on the ids) and the lens clause "under the report prompt vs the lookup prompt" cannot differ there; the question-first order is where surfacing on demand can show at the bridge word. The rule is applied per order. The agent's recommendation: Q47.10 is answered on the question-first order, the question-last order reported beside as the routes scenes as written; Dan decides. Gate: per order, each gated reader's (lookup, recall, report) read accuracy on its own unedited O prompts >= 0.80; the digit report's reported; an order where a gated reader fails is not tested; the job runs the competence first and stops with "not tested" (gate.json written, exit 0) if no order passes. Eligible: lookup, recall and report say and read O's and S's answers right. Change: h_S - h_O at the bridge word at L on each reader's own prompt (the lookup's serves all four in the question-last order), added on O. Parts: J++ = signed OMP, K = 25, over the J++ lens's letter-token atoms plus the ten digit tokens (the main test's letter-only restriction lifted; the ordinal words' four spellings are letter atoms, present on all three models: plan; the atoms picked per item in norms.jsonl); U = the 4 pointer directions (x0_massmean.subspaces Alf on muse30b_x0_probe_v4's states, not refit); random parts: X0's random subspace (seed 888 + L) at the part's share. Arms: none, whole, no_jpp, no_jpp_rand, no_alf, no_alf_rand, keep_alf, keep_alf_rand. Lens read: JLens.readout of O's bridge-word state at L (full vocabulary, special tokens out), the rank of O's slot's ordinal (the best of its four spellings) and of its slot digit; top-5 = rank <= 5; "the lens ranks ... in >= 0.4 of items" = the share of the order's items with top-5 rank under that reader's prompt. "Loses x of its switches without P beyond random" = X0's extra loss, Jdep - Rdep = (1 - S_noP / S_whole) - (1 - S_noP_rand / S_whole) over the order's items; the "without U" clause the same way against U's random part. Points from counts decide (EPS 1e-9 at the bars); cluster-bootstrap CIs over bridge items (10,000, seed 0) beside. A reader whose whole change switches fewer than 30 items (X0's VALID_N) has no interpretable loss: the order is not tested. Neither label: "neither". Control: the slot probe (x0_probe (b), ridge, the locker sentence's index, entities held out, 5 folds) on the stored bridge-word states per order and reader (the verdict stage). C0 sanity: Muse has no one-pick reference (x6_routes C0_REF); the question-last lookup's whole-change switch rate is recorded, descriptive. Scored by hand after Q47.10 is committed: scripts/x47_report.py verdict; view (10 random items per order, seed 0, the prompts as the model reads them, the bridge marked, every arm's answer, the lens's top-20); figures.
controls: the slot probe (x0_probe (b), entities held out) on the bridge-word states under each prompt: the address is there in both (verdict stage, from states.npz)
the report's read accuracy per true slot of the asked item's locker (gate.json): the report must track the slot, not say "first" (dumbest way 1)

the dictionary's ordinal atoms: the four spellings of first / second / third and the ten digits, present or absent (manifest; dumbest way 2), and the share of items whose 25 OMP atoms include one (norms.jsonl)
readers are separate prompts over the same context: the question-last prompts share every token through the bridge word (asserted per item), each reader's gate on its own prompt (dumbest way 3)
every removed or kept part against a random part of the same share (no_jpp_rand, no_alf_rand, keep_alf_rand)
the lookup and the recall read beside the report on the same items; the question-last lookup's whole-change switch rate recorded (no Muse one-pick reference)
n: 500 C0 scenes generated per order (plan on the Muse tokenizer, 28 Oct: 500 items, 32 bridge entities, none dropped by the encoding; O bridge in slot 1 / 2 / 3: 158 / 171 / 171); the first 200 eligible per order
notes: Batch 47, amendment 4 (Dan, 28 Oct ~03:00); queue position after 47.8 (9B): 47.10 (27B, Muse; 9B if its gate passes). SEALED: the job runs `run` only and writes manifest, plan, cases, competence, gate, outcomes, lens, norms, states.npz and 10 items' greedy texts per order; the log prints the counts and the gate, no switch rate. After Dan's Q47.10 is committed, by hand (CPU): uv run python scripts/x47_report.py verdict --runs qwen35_9b_x47_report x47_report_27b muse30_x47_report; view --name muse30_x47_report; figures --verdict <its folder>. Seeds: 0 the bootstrap and the examples, 888 + layer the random subspace, 2510 the routes scenes. warm_cusolver before the model loads (the 45k Muse cusolver failure). GPU estimate: the 27B's 2420 s (x47_10_27b.yaml, from x6_routes_r2 and x45p_27b in results/jobq/ledger_sesterce-h100x2.jsonl) scaled by Muse's x45p_muse / x45p_27b = 196 / 243 = 0.81 -> 1950 s = 0.54 GPU-h, rounded up to 0.7 (Dan's estimate ~1 GPU-h); a gate failure stops it after the competence, about 0.37 h.

title: Batch 47.8 on Muse (L26; every 4th layer L2-L50 (13 layers)): layer anatomy of the switch. Routes scenes (another item moved; the sanity swap), locker-first, split by bridge entity into a fit half and a test half; per layer the J++ / address (U_l) / identity-outside-J++ (I_l) parts of the bridge word's change, keep-only and without arms each against a random part of the same share, both readers, the probes and the refits; the D4 cache; SEALED until Q47.8
command: export BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_anatomy.py run --name muse30_x47_anatomy --why "batch 47, test 47.8 (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, amendment 2; Q47.8, sealed): layer anatomy of the switch on Muse, every 4th layer L2-L50 (13 layers), 200 test scenes"
question: As depth increases, what does a change at the bridge word move, and through which part: the lens-readable identity (the J++ part), the identity outside the lens (I_l), the address (U_l), or nothing? Does the lookup stop needing the lens part before or when it starts using the address (handoff), does the address form before it is used, does the identity leave the lens by L, and is the value never taken at any depth?
why_it_matters: The coarse version (Fig 6: 4-5 layers, J++ and position only) left the depth picture a candidate: Q35.1 held on the 9B and failed on the 27B by about 4 layers. One sweep with every part, both readers and the probes shows the around route forming layer by layer and turns Fig 6's "after the data" readings into the rule-based readings (a)-(d). Reported beside: the hall question's value share under every arm (count and share); "J++ at the key token matters" iff [position without the random part - position without J++] >= 0.30 (the same bar; expected not); only-U_num's random twin. D2: "the handover from the mention to the question" if l_R(recall) lies at or below the start of Zach's late band on the 9B and 27B (9B L26-29, 27B L52-60). As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before the run): Items: x47_cumulative's (the main test's X0 run at L, Muse's main-test X0 run (muse30b_x0_necessity, pre-merge name), its 200 scenes, the mixed ones in "all" only; the 45m clean-design run Muse's 45m run (muse30b_x45m_fresh, pre-merge name), its locker-first and locker-after scenes, its 96 mixed scenes left out for the budget), with x47_cumulative's asserts (O and S the same length, changed only at the bridge (clean) or the bridge and one token of the other person's pick (main); the asked pick sentence at the same positions with the same ids but the bridge's; the readers' prompts equal through the last patched context token). Order groups: x45m's (locker-first = the bridge's and S's bridge's locker sentences both before the asked pick; locker-after = both after). title: Batch 47.16 on the 9B (L12): does the address survive distance? Routes C2 scenes with k = 0 / 5 / 20 / 50 neutral sentences between the lockers and the picks; the gate per k (stop at the first failure); the whole change, without U vs random, x8's pointer swap at s = 2 vs random, the slot probe and the code's shift beta at the bridge word (sealed)
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_distance.py run --name qwen35_9b_x47_16 --why "batch 47, test 47.16 (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, amendment 5; Q47.16): x6_routes' C2 scenes with k neutral filler sentences between the locker sentences and the pick sentences, k = 0, 5, 20, 50 (the gate recomputed per k, stop at the first failure); at the bridge word: the whole change, without U against random, x8's pointer swap at s = 2 against a random direction, O's states for the slot probe and the code's shift beta; sealed"
question: Does the address at the bridge word survive distance from the locker sentences: as k neutral sentences separate the lockers from the picks, do the position share under the whole change, the slot probe and the pointer swap's success stay (distance-robust), does the lookup move from position to identity while still answering (address near, identity far), or does the model stop answering (breaks at k)? And does the code's shift beta stay <= 0.25 (Fig 8c at scale)?
why_it_matters: The pointer counts mentions, not tokens (Fig 8c: one neutral sentence shifts the code by beta ~ 0.15, not 1). A distance-robust address at 600 tokens says the lookup's route is an order code that does not decay with distance; a hand-over to identity at distance says the address is a near-field device; a break at some k bounds where any of this applies.

hypotheses.Q47.16: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q47.16: distance-robust / address near, identity far / breaks (at which k), on the 9B; on Muse); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x47_distance.py verdict / examples refuse until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.16): "Distance-robust address": position share and the probe within 0.10 of k = 0 at every k, swap success within 0.15. "Address near, identity far": position share falls >= 0.20 and identity rises by as much by k = 50 while accuracy stays >= 0.8. "Breaks": accuracy falls below the gate at some k (report the k; the test stops there). Also a check of Fig 8c at scale: the code's shift beta across k stays <= 0.25 (counts mentions, not tokens). AS COMPUTED (written before any run; Dan may override before the run; scripts/x47_distance.py docstring): SCENES: x6_routes' C2 scenes (its generator, seed 2510: the routes runs' own base scenes; the first 420 C2 candidates) with k neutral filler sentences between the last locker sentence and the first pick sentence of O and S alike, k in {0, 5, 20, 50}. Fillers: a fixed pool of 60 sentences (no item, person, digit, number word, locker / pick / hall wording; checked against the target's pools in the plan and in the run); per base scene one seeded draw (seed 4716 keyed by the scene) of 50, of which the first k are inserted, so the blocks nest (k = 5 is a prefix of k = 20 is a prefix of k = 50). Each variant re-encoded with x6_routes.encode (the bridge word one token at one index shared by O and S; both readers' prompts the same through it; else dropped and counted; plan check: none dropped). GATE per k, in order 0, 5, 20, 50: X0's competence on every candidate at k (8 greedy tokens and the read, unedited O and S, both readers); O's read accuracy >= 0.80 per reader; at the first failing k the job records it (gate.json stopped_at) and skips the larger ks. CHOSEN: the first 300 base scenes (generation order) eligible at every k that passed (both readers say and read O's and S's answers right), so the k cells are paired. ARMS at each passed k (on O, at the bridge word at L12, both readers): none; whole (Delta = h_S - h_O); without U (the fresh-scene pointer basis, x0_massmean.subspaces' Alf on qwen35_9b_x0_probe_v4, not refit) and without a random part of U's share (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L); x8_write's pointer swap at s = 2, h + 2 (mu_t - mu_j) for both other slots t (j = the bridge's locker slot in O; mu = pointer_means, not refit), each against a random direction of the same norm (seed 4717 keyed by the scene and t). Lookup answers classified identity / position / value / original / other (x6_routes) and, under the swap, target / original / third / other (x8_write). why_it_matters: The routes test says the lookup keeps an address at the bridge word, never the number, when the question comes last (value 0 of 300 on four models). If the model prefetches the number once it knows the question, 'never the value' is a fact about question order, not about the representation; and whether a prefetched value lives in the J-space tests the workspace account's 'surfaced to the J-space on demand'. 'Address regardless' is the stronger version of 'never the value'.

<q> <instruction>'; the instruction block moves with the question). With the question first the two readers' prompts differ before the bridge, so the change is computed per reader from its own prompts (question-last: one change from the lookup's prompt, read by both). command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP= BJ_DAS_GDN=torch; uv run python scripts/x48_das.py run --name qwen35_9b_x48_das_r2 --why "batch 48, test 48.1 (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml; Q48.1): DAS at the bridge word at L12 on the main test's locker-first pairs the whole change switches; one R per reader and k, random and shuffled-target baselines; sealed"
question: At the bridge word at L12, is there a low-dimensional subspace of the change that mediates the lookup, one that mediates the recall, are they disjoint (own-IIA high, cross-IIA low), and where do they sit against the lens (J++-25), the pointer directions U and the input-embedding part W_E-25?
why_it_matters: We know what the lookup's identity code is not (not J++ at K = 25, not W_E at K = 100, not the layer's main directions). A learned subspace that mediates the lookup, measured against the lens, U and W_E, says what it is, with how many dimensions, and whether it is disjoint from the recall's.

hypotheses.Q48.1: Dan's answers in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q48.1, one option and a confidence per letter (a)-(d)); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x48_das.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch48.yaml, 48.1): (a) two readers, two subspaces: own-IIA >= 0.7 at some k <= 16 for both readers and cross-IIA <= 0.25 in both directions (paired CI excluding overlap with own-IIA); (b) the recall's subspace is the lens's part: R_recall's energy inside J++-25 >= 0.5 (random R <= 0.15), R_lookup's <= 0.2; (c) the address is part of the lookup's subspace: ||R_lookup^T U||_F^2 / 4 >= 0.5 (random R ~ k/d); (d) a third identity code: R_lookup's energy outside (J++-25 u U u W_E-25) >= 0.5 while its own-IIA >= 0.7, and R_lookup alone gives identity answers >= 0.3 in the routes read. Fallback: if own-IIA stays < 0.5 at k = 64 for the lookup, "no low-dimensional mediator at this token and layer". As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override): pairs = the stored main-test run's (qwen35_9b_x0_necessity, chat, L12) eligible scenes that are locker-first (both items' locker sentences before the asked pick, x0_strata) and that the stored whole change switches for at least one reader; each reader trains and is read on the pairs the whole change switches for it (lookup 72, recall 75 of 75; the scene ids in pairs.json). Split by the original bridge entity 60 / 20 / 20 (train / select k / test), seed 0 (32 entities: 19 / 6 / 7; lookup pairs 44 / 10 / 18, recall 46 / 10 / 19). Intervention h <- h_O + R R^T (h_S - h_O) at the bridge token at L12 on the O prompt, R [d x k] with orthonormal columns (torch.nn.utils.parametrizations.orthogonal); loss = cross-entropy of S's answer's first token at X0's chat read position (the appended space); Adam lr 1e-3, 300 steps, batch 16 (micro-batches of 8, gradient accumulation); h_O / h_S cached once per pair, the training forwards real (the layers after L12 are needed for the loss), the IIA evaluated with X0's read (generate_batch, the AddRows edit). Chosen k per reader = the smallest k <= 16 whose select-split own-IIA >= 0.7, else the k with the highest select own-IIA; every rule read at the chosen k on the test entities' pairs: point estimates = means over the reader's test pairs, cluster-bootstrap CIs over bridge entities (10,000, seed 0) beside them. "Paired CI excluding overlap with own-IIA" = the paired bootstrap of own-IIA minus cross-IIA over the reader's test pairs has a lower bound > 0; cross-IIA for a reader = its switch rate under the other reader's R at that reader's chosen k. Energy inside a part = the share of ||R R^T Delta||^2 in the span of the pair's 25 signed-OMP J++ atoms (J++-25; also 100), of its 25 W_E atoms (x0_necessity's "we" dictionary), or of U (x0_massmean.subspaces' Alf on qwen35_9b_x0_probe_v4, rank 4); outside = 1 minus the share in the orthonormalised union of the three; cos^2 with U = ||R^T U||_F^2 / rank(U) (x6_routes.mean_cos2; a random R: k / d). The routes read: R_lookup alone (at the chosen k) written on the first 100 eligible x6_routes C2 scenes (another item moved); identity answers = the lookup's top token is the new item's own locker digit. IIA divided by the whole change's rerun switch rate on the test pairs reported beside. Energy >= 0.8 of Delta flags the R "not selective". Scored by hand: scripts/x48_das.py verdict (EPS 1e-9 at the bars).

question: Is the pointer item-agnostic: does U, the address directions fit on animal scenes, carry the lookup's position route on scenes whose items are fruits or people's names as it does on animals (without U cuts position answers >= 0.3 beyond random, within 0.1 of the animal result; only U sends >= 0.15 of lookups to the position), or is the code slot x type (only a U' refit on that type's scenes does)?
why_it_matters: The pointer is read as an address, not as part of the item's identity (47.0: not verbalizable; 45a / 45e: layout-free, item-specific controls fail). An address should not care what is stored at it. If U transfers to objects and names unchanged, the slot code is one code for any item; if only a per-type refit works, the "address" is entangled with the item type and the account needs a weaker word.

's pick?", a one-word read), names (suite_v1's 59 one-token people's names as the items, "The locker of Alice is 5." / "Iris picked Alice.", the three items never among the scene's three pickers; no attribute fact exists for a name, so the recall is skipped and said so). Matched: per scene index the five digits, the three people, the slot order and the pick order come from one shared stream (seed 4711); only the items come from the type's own stream. Gate 0.80 per reader per type: O's read accuracy (X0's chat read: the digit's space token appended for a digit reader, nothing for the word reader) over the type's generated scenes; the items are the first 300 scenes in generator order on which the lookup says and reads O's and S's answers right (a failed lookup gate = the type is "not tested"); the recall is read on those of them it gets right too, where its gate passed (reported, not in the rule; a failed recall gate does not stop the lookup test). Arms at the bridge word at L12 (Δ = h_S - h_O added on O; switch = the top token is S's answer's first token; the lookup's top token classified identity / position / value / original / other): whole; no_alf = Δ - U U^T Δ vs no_alf_rand = Δ minus a random part of U's share of ||Δ||^2 (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L); keep_alf = U U^T Δ vs keep_alf_rand. U = x47_atoms.pointer_basis (x0_massmean's layout-free mass-mean slot directions on the probe's fresh animal scenes, qwen35_9b_x0_probe_v4; never refit). The fallback, always computed, read only where the rule fails: per type a seeded split (seed 4712) of the chosen items into a fit half and a test half; U' = x0_massmean.mass_mean of O's bridge-word states by the O bridge's locker slot on the fit half (rank 2); no_refit / no_refit_rand / keep_refit / keep_refit_rand read on the test half only. Reading: per type, position share = the share of its lookup items whose top token is the position route's digit; fall = position share(no_alf_rand) - position share(no_alf), paired cluster bootstrap over the O bridge item (10,000, seed 0) beside the point; the animal result = the same job's animal type (the stored routes run qwen35_9b_x6_routes_keeponly, fall 0.46, only-U 0.26, reported beside). question: When the address at the bridge word is swapped (x8_write's mu_k - mu_j at s = 2), does the question's attention move onto the locker sentence of the written slot k, and does a head that moves carry the switch (zeroing it undoes it)?
why_it_matters: The address is probe-readable, removable and writable; nothing yet shows who dereferences it. A head whose attention follows the written address, and without which the switch falls, puts the dereference in hand at the head level; on the 9B three of four layers are Gated DeltaNet, so a null here may only say "not in full attention".

hypotheses.Q49.7: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q49.7, per model: (a) follows / (b) elsewhere / (c) neither; if (a), above L+4 or within 4 layers of L); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x49_attn.py verdict and view refuse until the Dan: line is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch49.yaml, 49.7, with amendment 2, Dan 28 Oct ~14:20). Read half, decisive query site the last token (the question tokens' mean beside, the same rules), cluster bootstrap over bridge entities (10,000, seed 0), EPS 1e-9 at the bars. move = (mass on slot k's sentence - mass on slot j's) under the arm minus the same under none, per head and (item, k); j = the bridge item's slot, k = the written slot; a sentence's mass = all its tokens. "The attention follows the address": on the pairs where the lookup switched to slot k's locker under the swap, >= 1 of the five candidate heads has mean move >= 0.30 with its CI excluding 0, its mean move under the random vector on the same pairs <= 0.05, and its mean move on the non-switched swap pairs <= 0.10. "Dereference elsewhere": the switch share >= 0.3 and no recorded head (every full-attention layer > L, every head) reaches a mean move of 0.15 on the switched pairs. Otherwise neither. (1) Aggregate, beside the per-head rule: the summed move over the five candidates and over every head of the best head's layer; "distributed dereference" if either sum >= 0.30 while no single candidate reaches 0.30. (2) Necessity: the best head (chosen on the fit half before the ablation runs) has its output (its slice of o_proj's input) zeroed at the last token, and separately at the question tokens, under the swap on the read half; "the head carries the position route" if the switch to slot k falls by >= 0.5 of its swap value while the identity answers (read pairs answering slot j's locker under the swap) change <= 0.10 and the recall's answer changes <= 0.10 (swap + zero vs swap); the clean answers lost (none + zero vs none) beside. (3) Weights-level, descriptive: S[k, k'] = (W_Q mu^q_k)^T (W_K mu^src_k') for the best head, mu^q_k = the mean last-token attention input (post input-norm) over items whose picked item is in slot k, mu^src_k' = the mean over items of the mean input at slot k''s locker-sentence tokens, unedited; diagonal dominance = (mean diagonal - mean off-diagonal) / SD of the off-diagonal; RoPE and the q/k norms left out (said so); the actual mean attention logits on slot j's / k's / the third sentence's tokens under none / swap / random beside. (4) The 9B caveat: if "elsewhere" holds here (three of four layers are Gated DeltaNet), the verdict writes "the dereference is not in full attention on this model" and Muse decides. Report beside: the best head's layer and index (and L + how many), its attention entropy per arm, the per-token breakdown of its mass on slot k's sentence (item / number / rest), the total full-attention change (the summed move over every head; the mean total-variation distance from none over every head, swap vs random). question: Is the pointer item-agnostic: does U, the address directions fit on animal scenes, carry the lookup's position route on scenes whose items are fruits or people's names as it does on animals (without U cuts position answers >= 0.3 beyond random, within 0.1 of the animal result; only U sends >= 0.15 of lookups to the position), or is the code slot x type (only a U' refit on that type's scenes does)?
why_it_matters: The pointer is read as an address, not as part of the item's identity (47.0: not verbalizable; 45a / 45e: layout-free, item-specific controls fail). An address should not care what is stored at it. If U transfers to objects and names unchanged, the slot code is one code for any item; if only a per-type refit works, the "address" is entangled with the item type and the account needs a weaker word. On Muse the stored animal fall is 0.27, under the rule's 0.3 bar: the in-job animal reference says whether that is the design or the model.

Matched: per scene index the five digits, the three people, the slot order and the pick order come from one shared stream (seed 4711); only the items come from the type's own stream. why_it_matters: The address is probe-readable, removable and writable; nothing yet shows who dereferences it. A head whose attention follows the written address, and without which the switch falls, puts the dereference in hand at the head level; on Muse every layer is softmax attention, so Muse decides what a 9B null means.

hypotheses.Q49.7: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q49.7, per model: (a) follows / (b) elsewhere / (c) neither; if (a), above L+4 or within 4 layers of L); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x49_attn.py verdict and view refuse until the Dan: line is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch49.yaml, 49.7, with amendment 2, Dan 28 Oct ~14:20). Read half, decisive query site the last token (the question tokens' mean beside, the same rules), cluster bootstrap over bridge entities (10,000, seed 0), EPS 1e-9 at the bars. move = (mass on slot k's sentence - mass on slot j's) under the arm minus the same under none, per head and (item, k); j = the bridge item's slot, k = the written slot; a sentence's mass = all its tokens. "The attention follows the address": on the pairs where the lookup switched to slot k's locker under the swap, >= 1 of the five candidate heads has mean move >= 0.30 with its CI excluding 0, its mean move under the random vector on the same pairs <= 0.05, and its mean move on the non-switched swap pairs <= 0.10. "Dereference elsewhere": the switch share >= 0.3 and no recorded head (every layer > L, every head) reaches a mean move of 0.15 on the switched pairs. Otherwise neither. (1) Aggregate, beside the per-head rule: the summed move over the five candidates and over every head of the best head's layer; "distributed dereference" if either sum >= 0.30 while no single candidate reaches 0.30. (2) Necessity: the best head (chosen on the fit half before the ablation runs) has its output (its slice of o_proj's input) zeroed at the last token, and separately at the question tokens, under the swap on the read half; "the head carries the position route" if the switch to slot k falls by >= 0.5 of its swap value while the identity answers (read pairs answering slot j's locker under the swap) change <= 0.10 and the recall's answer changes <= 0.10 (swap + zero vs swap); the clean answers lost (none + zero vs none) beside. (3) Weights-level, descriptive: S[k, k'] = (W_Q mu^q_k)^T (W_K mu^src_k') for the best head, mu^q_k = the mean last-token attention input (post input-norm) over items whose picked item is in slot k, mu^src_k' = the mean over items of the mean input at slot k''s locker-sentence tokens, unedited; diagonal dominance = (mean diagonal - mean off-diagonal) / SD of the off-diagonal; RoPE and the q/k norms left out (said so); the actual mean attention logits on slot j's / k's / the third sentence's tokens under none / swap / random beside. R_pos (k = 2, 4, 8) trained on routes position counterfactuals (same item, its locker sentence moved to another slot; target = O's locker at that slot); own-IIA, U's and W's energy inside R_pos, R_pos inside J++-25, the recall's cross read; random and shuffled-target baselines

question: At the bridge word at L12, does a learned low-dimensional subspace R_pos mediate the locker sentence's position (moving the lookup to the locker at the slot the bridge's sentence occupies in S), and is it the hand-built address U (and/or 47.2's slot subspace W), leaving the recall alone?
why_it_matters: The address U is probe-readable, removable and writable, but it was built by hand (mass means by slot). If DAS, which is free to find any subspace, recovers U, the address is validated as the model's own mediator; if it finds a mediator that U misses, there are two address codes; if none, the position route has no low-dimensional mediator at this token and layer.

hypotheses.Q49.8: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q49.8, (a)-(d) at k = 4); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x49_das_pos.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch49.yaml, 49.8): "the learned address is ours" if at k = 4 >= 0.6 of U's energy lies in R_pos (random k/d ~ 0.001) with own-IIA >= 0.6 and the recall's cross-IIA <= 0.1; "two address codes" if own-IIA >= 0.6 but U's energy in R_pos <= 0.2 (then report which one the writes used, 47.2's slot-specific result, and the angle between them); Q49.8 (c) "no low-dimensional mediator" if own-IIA < 0.6; (d) "in between" otherwise. As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the enqueue): pairs = the stored routes run qwen35_9b_x6_routes (chat, L12, scene seed 2510), its 300 eligible C1 scenes (the bridge's locker sentence swapped with another slot's, the bridge's number a new digit in S; the item is the same in O and S), restricted to the 187 whose stored whole change sent the lookup to the position answer (identity 109, other 4 dropped, counted in pairs.json); the counterfactual answer = O's locker digit at the slot the bridge's sentence occupies in S (x6_routes' expect["position"]), not S's own answer. Scenes rebuilt with the tokenizer and asserted equal to the stored ids. Split by bridge entity 60 / 20 / 20 (train / select / test), seed 0 (31 entities: 19 / 6 / 6; pairs 112 / 41 / 34). Intervention h <- h_O + R R^T (h_S - h_O) at the bridge token at L12 on the O prompt (x48_das's code: R [d x k] orthonormal via torch.nn.utils.parametrizations.orthogonal, Adam lr 1e-3, 300 steps, batch 16 in micro-batches of 8, cross-entropy of the position answer's token at X0's chat read position); one R_pos per k in {2, 4, 8}, one untrained random R and one shuffled-target R per k. question: 3b and 47.4 put the lookup's link in the locker sentences, made before L; 48.3 found no "who picked it" at the item or number token. In locker-after clean scenes, is a person mark distributed over the locker sentence (read pooled, not at any one token), is it a picked-flag rather than a person, or neither at the sentence?
why_it_matters: It closes 48.3 against 3b: either the binding is at the locker sentence but spread over its tokens (48.3 looked at two tokens only), or the sentence marks "picked by the one who will be asked" (a flag, not a name), or the link is made elsewhere, and the README's "no forward binding" line is rewritten from the result.

hypotheses.Q49.3: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q49.3); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no probe in the job (scripts/x49_probe.py verdict and view refuse until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch49.yaml, 49.3): "Distributed person mark": pooled (i) >= 0.85 with every per-token (i) <= 0.6. "A picked-flag, not a person": (ii) >= 0.85 pooled or at some token while (i) <= 0.5. "Neither at the sentence": both at chance; the link is made elsewhere; D1's locker-after map is the evidence. As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before the run): scenes = the 9B's clean-design run (qwen35_9b_x45m_fresh, x0_necessity --alt fresh), its chat scenes at L12, built by 48.3's scene_item; groups by x45m.group_of (locker-after = the rule's scenes, locker-first = the control, mixed = training rows only); only O (the lookup's prompt) is read. States at L // 2 = 6 and L = 12, at every token overlapping each locker sentence with a picker (its period included) and their mean ('pooled'); each token keyed by its role ('w:The', 'w:locker', 'w:of', 'w:the', 'item', 'w:is', 'w:space', 'number', 'w:.'). Probes (48.3's ridge: standardized features, the penalty by an inner CV, out-of-fold over 5 folds, seed 0), trained and scored within a stratum (the sentence after / before its picker's pick), per key and pooled, at each layer: (i) the picker, the best of the scene's three names (chance 1/3), folds by the sentence's item; rule cell = the bridge item's sentence in locker-after scenes, the other items' sentences beside; (ii) picked by the asked person (binary), folds by the sentence's item, balanced accuracy (chance 0.5) with the rule cell's rows as the positives and the stratum's other items' sentences as the negatives; (iii) the item's identity on the mean, the scene's four locker items as candidates, folds by the picker (the person held out; descriptive, the pooled read's positive control). "Every per-token" = the keys present in >= half of the rule cell's rows; "(i) <= 0.5" = every (i) cell, pooled and per key; "at chance" = point <= chance + 0.10; the locker-first control (the same probes, 'before' stratum, locker-first scenes) must be at chance for (i) and (ii), else a distributed / flag label reads "not interpretable (control above chance)", the raw label beside. Per layer on points (EPS 1e-9); the model is distributed (flag) if it holds at L or L // 2, neither if neither at both, else in between. Cluster-bootstrap CIs over the sentence's item (10,000, seed 0) beside every accuracy. Scored by hand: scripts/x49_probe.py verdict; view; story_b49c.build_pooled.
controls: locker-first scenes: the same probes where the bridge sentence precedes the asked pick (must be at chance for (i) and (ii))
the other items' locker sentences: (i) on them beside the rule cell; they are (ii)'s negatives
(iii) the item's identity on the sentence mean: the pooled read carries the sentence's content (positive control)
per-token beside pooled: the rule needs the pooled read without any single token
the person names are the generator's pickers (scene_facts) and must match the pick sentences; a scene whose bridge item or number is not one token is dropped and counted

question: On Zach's passages, with the bridge named in a pointer sentence, does the lookup (K final: the fact stated) go around the J++ part of the change at the bridge while the recall (M final: the fact from memory) needs it, and does the lookup switch more when the bridge's fact sentence comes before the pointer sentence?
why_it_matters: Zach's knock-out ran on our locker scenes; our change-removal on his passages closes the 2x2 (operation x dataset). If the split holds on his natural passages, it is not a property of our locker layout; if the lookup follows the lens here, the split is a scene artefact.

hypotheses.Q50.1: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q50.1); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x50_zach.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch50.yaml, Z1, verbatim): per model, gap >= 0.3 and lookup extra loss <= 0.10 -> "the split holds on his passages"; lookup >= 0.20 -> "the lookup follows the lens here"; else in between. Order split (after the gate, before the data): items where the bridge's fact sentence comes before the pointer sentence vs after. "The order pattern replicates" if the lookup's switch under the whole change is >= 2x higher fact-first than fact-after (both CIs), as in our 65-89 % vs 9-19 %. Hard-read stratum (v3 flag): the gap within hard-read items within 0.15 of the easy items -> "not a lookup-difficulty effect". As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before it). Items: v3 is not on the box, so Zach's v2 facts module, jsuite_v2_test_chat (seed 2601, his main set), and jsuite_v2nb_test_chat (his second seed) only if fewer than 200 passages are eligible on the main set. A passage = one of his P-start scenes: its PK item (all entities' true facts stated: our lookup, reader K) and its PM item (the bridge's fact not stated, the others carry fictional values: our recall, reader M), same question and answer, same pointer / filler sentences in the same order. Leak filter: a description holding its answer or a derived word (jsuite_v2_tables.DERIV) is dropped (none of v2's 361 descriptions does). S: the asked person's pointer sentence names another entity of the passage whose true fact the K passage states and whose answer differs (the first, in a seeded order per scene (seed 5001), whose name ends at the same token index; only the name's tokens change); nothing else changes. Plan check on the Qwen tokenizer: 358 passages, 270 aligned (88 dropped: no candidate aligns), strata 133 fact-first / 137 fact-after; second seed 274 more. The read: his chat framing (one user turn, thinking off, no prefill), the top token against the answer's first token (his correct_top); switch = the other entity's answer (K: its stated fact; M: its memory fact, the same word). Gate: O's read accuracy >= 0.80 per reader over every aligned passage whose competence ran; eligible: both readers say (8 greedy tokens) and read O's and S's answers right; the first 200 in passage order. The reads run whatever the gate says; a failed gate is "not tested" in the verdict (the gate over Zach's competence-kept passages is recorded beside). Delta = h_S - h_O at the name's last token at L12, per reader (the K and M passages differ before it), added on O. Arms: whole; without J++ (signed OMP, k = 25, the letter-token J++ atoms at L, the pinned lens); without a random part of its share (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L). Extra loss = X0's excess (S_no_jpp_rand - S_no_jpp) / S_whole; gap = M's minus K's on the same cluster-bootstrap draws (bridge entity, 10,000, seed 0). Order strata by the original bridge's fact sentence vs the pointer sentence in the K passage (x0_split_by_order's convention; the other entity's order recorded beside); replicates iff fact-first >= 2 x fact-after (point estimates; both intervals beside and whether they separate). Hard-read: no flag in v2, not tested. Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9); an undefined extra loss holds no clause. Scored by hand: scripts/x50_zach.py verdict --part z1.

title: Batch 51.1 on the 9B (L12): dose curves with a matched random part at every dose. At the bridge word, the change's J++ part alone at alpha in {0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3} and the rest alone at beta in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5} (with and without the address), each against a random part of the same share at the same gain; J(1,1) for the loss bar; 49.1's locker-first main-test items, both readers
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x51_dose.py run --name qwen35_9b_x51_1 --why "Batch 51, test 51.1 (jobs/c3/batch51.yaml; Q51.1): dose curves at L12, alpha P_J Delta (alpha 0.5..3) and beta (Delta - P_J Delta) with and without U (beta 0.25..1.5), each with its random twin of the same share at the same gain, J(1,1) and J(0,0); 49.1's items (main-test locker-first scenes of qwen35_9b_x0_necessity); sealed"
question: Does the lookup stay blind to the change's J++ part at every dose under the loss bar, and does the recall read the J++ part above its share? Each reader's switch as a function of one part's gain, against a random part of the same share at the same gain.
why_it_matters: 49.1 compared the parts at gains 0..2 with random parts only at four corners; a blind lookup at one dose could be a dose too small. Dose curves with a matched random part at every dose separate "the lookup cannot read the J++ part" from "the J++ part is too small at gain 1", and give the readers' relative weights on the two parts (the fit's b/a).

hypotheses.Q51.1: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q51.1: (i) per model 9B / 27B / Muse; (ii) per model; (iii) Muse yes / no); not committed when this spec was written, so the job is sealed: per-item outputs only, no verdict; scripts/x51_dose.py verdict and view refuse until the answer is committed.

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch51.yaml, 51.1), verbatim: (i) "The lookup is blind to the J++ part": switch minus random <= 0.10 at every alpha whose plain-text loss stays under 2x the whole change's -- on all three. (ii) "The recall reads the J++ part above its share": at the first alpha where the J++ part alone switches >= 0.3, J minus random >= 0.2 -- per model. (iii) "Together only" (Muse): (1,1) from 49.1 >= 0.8 while the best single-part dose under the loss bar stays <= 0.3. Output: one figure, four curves per model (two readers x two parts), random dashed, the loss bar marked; a per-model, per-reader fit logit(switch) = a alpha + b beta (+ c alpha beta), report b/a and whether c is needed. As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the verdict): items, layer and parts are 49.1's (scripts/x49_gain.py, imported): the main test's eligible items of qwen35_9b_x0_necessity at L12 (chat; X0's gate 0.80 per reader on O unedited and >= 150 eligible, asserted from its gate.json), rebuilt by x47_cumulative.select, locker-first only: 75 items, 32 bridge items, the same items in the same order as qwen35_9b_x49_1 (plan in results/x51_dose/plan-20261028T162252Z). Delta = h_S - h_O at the bridge word at L; P_J Delta = X0's 25-atom signed OMP part over the J++ letter-token atoms at L; R Delta = X0's random part at P_J Delta's share of ||Delta||^2 (random basis seed 888 + L); U = x47_atoms.pointer_basis (rank 4, never refit), R_U Delta the random part at U U^T Delta's share. Arms (added at the bridge word at L on O, X0's AddRows; 32 arms): J(alpha,0) = alpha P_J Delta and its twin R(alpha,0) = alpha R Delta; J(0,beta) = beta (Delta - P_J Delta) and its twin R(0,beta) = beta (Delta - R Delta) (the random complement at the rest's share, 49.1's R(0,b)); without the address J(0,beta)-U = beta (Delta - P_J Delta - U U^T Delta) (49.1's J(0,2)-U at gain beta, as written) and its twin J(0,beta)-RU = beta (Delta - P_J Delta - R_U Delta); J(1,1) = Delta and J(0,0) = O unedited. The J and R arms are computed with 49.1's expression, so the cells both tests share are the same floats. Switch = X0's chat read (top token = S's answer's first token). Plain-text loss = 49.1's: -log p(O's token after the bridge word) at the bridge word, O's lookup prompt cut after the bridge word; the loss bar: an arm is under it when its mean loss over the items <= 2 x J(1,1)'s mean loss (this run's J(1,1)). (i) is read on the lookup, J(alpha,0) - R(alpha,0) at every alpha whose J(alpha,0) is under the bar; no alpha under the bar = undecided; "on all three" = yes on each of the three models. (ii) is read on the recall (the lookup beside): the first alpha in ascending order with J(alpha,0) >= 0.3; it is not conditioned on the loss bar (whether that alpha is under it is reported); no alpha reaching 0.3 = no. (iii) is decisive on Muse's recall (the lookup and the 9B / 27B beside): (1,1) = the stored 49.1 run's J(1,1) switch rate on the same items (results/x49_gain/<run>/outcomes.jsonl); single parts = J(alpha,0) and J(0,beta) under the bar (the -U arms are reported, not counted); no single dose under the bar = undecided. Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9 at the bars); cluster-bootstrap CIs over the bridge items (10,000, seed 0) beside, paired for J minus random. Fit (descriptive): binomial logistic regression with an intercept, logit(switch) = a0 + a alpha + b beta (+ c alpha beta) (the intercept added because O unedited does not switch; without it the fit puts O at 0.5), on every J cell with the address of this run (alpha axis, beta axis, (1,1), (0,0)) plus 49.1's 5x5 grid cells on the same items that this run does not repeat (16 cells; 28 cells in all), Newton-IRLS with an L2 penalty of 1.0 on a, b, c (not a0) so a reader that never switches along one axis keeps finite coefficients; b/a from the additive fit; "c is needed" when c's 95% cluster-bootstrap CI (the same 10,000 draws over bridge items, seed 0) excludes 0; the naive likelihood-ratio statistic (reads treated as independent, anti-conservative) beside. Code: scripts/x51_dose.py verdict (rule_blind, rule_above, rule_together, logistic_fit; figure dose_curves.png) and view (verify pack).

the lookup on the identical edits

(ii) "The recall reads the J++ part above its share": at the first alpha where the J++ part alone switches >= 0.3, J minus random >= 0.2 -- per model. Output: one figure, four curves per model (two readers x two parts), random dashed, the loss bar marked; a per-model, per-reader fit logit(switch) = a alpha + b beta (+ c alpha beta), report b/a and whether c is needed. As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the verdict): items, layer and parts are 49.1's (scripts/x49_gain.py, imported): the main test's eligible items of x0_necessity_27b_chat at L32 (chat; X0's gate 0.80 per reader on O unedited and >= 150 eligible, asserted from its gate.json), rebuilt by x47_cumulative.select, locker-first only: 69 items, 34 bridge items, the same items in the same order as x49_1_27b (plan in results/x51_dose/plan-20261028T162254Z). Delta = h_S - h_O at the bridge word at L; P_J Delta = X0's 25-atom signed OMP part over the J++ letter-token atoms at L; R Delta = X0's random part at P_J Delta's share of ||Delta||^2 (random basis seed 888 + L); U = x47_atoms.pointer_basis (rank 4, never refit), R_U Delta the random part at U U^T Delta's share. Arms (added at the bridge word at L on O, X0's AddRows; 32 arms): J(alpha,0) = alpha P_J Delta and its twin R(alpha,0) = alpha R Delta; J(0,beta) = beta (Delta - P_J Delta) and its twin R(0,beta) = beta (Delta - R Delta) (the random complement at the rest's share, 49.1's R(0,b)); without the address J(0,beta)-U = beta (Delta - P_J Delta - U U^T Delta) (49.1's J(0,2)-U at gain beta, as written) and its twin J(0,beta)-RU = beta (Delta - P_J Delta - R_U Delta); J(1,1) = Delta and J(0,0) = O unedited. The J and R arms are computed with 49.1's expression, so the cells both tests share are the same floats. Switch = X0's chat read (top token = S's answer's first token). Plain-text loss = 49.1's: -log p(O's token after the bridge word) at the bridge word, O's lookup prompt cut after the bridge word; the loss bar: an arm is under it when its mean loss over the items <= 2 x J(1,1)'s mean loss (this run's J(1,1)). (i) is read on the lookup, J(alpha,0) - R(alpha,0) at every alpha whose J(alpha,0) is under the bar; no alpha under the bar = undecided; "on all three" = yes on each of the three models. (ii) is read on the recall (the lookup beside): the first alpha in ascending order with J(alpha,0) >= 0.3; it is not conditioned on the loss bar (whether that alpha is under it is reported); no alpha reaching 0.3 = no. Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9 at the bars); cluster-bootstrap CIs over the bridge items (10,000, seed 0) beside, paired for J minus random. Fit (descriptive): binomial logistic regression with an intercept, logit(switch) = a0 + a alpha + b beta (+ c alpha beta) (the intercept added because O unedited does not switch; without it the fit puts O at 0.5), on every J cell with the address of this run (alpha axis, beta axis, (1,1), (0,0)) plus 49.1's 5x5 grid cells on the same items that this run does not repeat (16 cells; 28 cells in all), Newton-IRLS with an L2 penalty of 1.0 on a, b, c (not a0) so a reader that never switches along one axis keeps finite coefficients; b/a from the additive fit; "c is needed" when c's 95% cluster-bootstrap CI (the same 10,000 draws over bridge items, seed 0) excludes 0; the naive likelihood-ratio statistic (reads treated as independent, anti-conservative) beside. question: Does the lookup stay blind to the change's J++ part at every dose under the loss bar, and does the recall read the J++ part above its share? Each reader's switch as a function of one part's gain, against a random part of the same share at the same gain.
why_it_matters: 49.1 compared the parts at gains 0..2 with random parts only at four corners; a blind lookup at one dose could be a dose too small. title: Batch 51.7 on the 9B (L12): Z1 on the full carrier. On Z1's passages (Zach's jsuite v2, named bridge), the bridge name's last token set to S's state at every block <= L (whole), minus the J++ part of each layer's change (layer l's own 25 atoms), minus a random part of the same share; both readers, both strata, plain-text loss per arm; Z1's one-layer arms beside from its stored rows; sealed
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x51_carrier.py run --name qwen35_9b_x51_7
question: On Zach's passages the whole change at the bridge name's last token at one layer redirects only part of the lookups, least where the bridge's fact sentence comes after the pointer sentence. With the change written at the name's last token at every layer <= L (so later tokens read S's name below L too), do fact-after lookups rise by >= 0.3 (the slice explanation), and on this full carrier does the lookup still go around the J++ part while the recall needs it?
why_it_matters: Z1 read the split at one layer at one token. The order and token-map results predict that later tokens read the name below L; if so, the one-layer change is a slice of the carrier, and the split must be read on the whole carrier before it counts for Zach's passages. If the lookup follows the lens once the carrier is whole, the one-layer split was a slice artefact.

hypotheses.Q51.7: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q51.7); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x51_carrier.py verdict / view refuse until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch51.yaml, 51.7, verbatim): (i) "The slice explanation": the whole before-L raises the lookup's switch on fact-after items by >= 0.3 over the one-layer whole, and on fact-first brings the lookup within 0.10 of the recall. (ii) On the full carrier, per model and reported per stratum with fact-first decisive: recall extra loss - lookup extra loss >= 0.3 and lookup <= 0.10 -> "the split holds on the full carrier"; lookup >= 0.20 -> "the lookup follows the lens on the full carrier"; else in between. (iii) If fact-after lookups stay under 0.5 even under whole before-L: "the link is made away from the bridge token" -- only then the window-patching read (the bridge token at layers <= L plus the bridge's fact sentence), 50 items, descriptive. As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before it). Items: Z1's chosen passages in Z1's order (results/x50_zach/qwen35_9b_x50_z1/gate.json: 200, 100 fact-first / 100 fact-after, 182 from jsuite_v2_test_chat and 18 from jsuite_v2nb_test_chat), rebuilt with x50_zach.z1_cases on the 9B tokenizer and equal to Z1's stored cases (ids, patch token, answer tokens, S's entity, stratum; 0 mismatches at plan time); a mismatch fails the job. Z1's gate decides tested / not tested (numbers descriptive only on a failed gate). Read: Z1's (his chat framing, no prefill; switch = the top token is the other entity's answer's first token). Arms on O, per reader (the K and M passages differ before the patch token): whole_bL = the patch token (the name's last token) set (SetRows, not added) to h_S,l at every block output l = 0..12; no_jpp_bL = set to h_S,l - P_J,l Delta_l, Delta_l = h_S,l - h_O,l from clean S and O forwards, P_J,l = x0_necessity.fit(layer l's letter-token J++ atoms, Delta_l, 25, signed); rand_bL = set to h_S,l - statement_positions.random_subspace_part(Delta_l, P_J,l Delta_l's share of ||Delta_l||^2, X0's random basis seed 888 + l). The input embedding is not edited in these three arms (the lens has no map there and the arms stay matched); whole_emb (= whole_bL with S's token id at the patch token, 47.4's (b)) is read beside, descriptive. At L the three before-L states equal Z1's one-layer states (h_O,L + its vector), so the difference from Z1's arms is what later tokens read below L. Z1's one-layer arms (whole, no_jpp, no_jpp_rand at L12) are read from its stored outcomes, not rerun; O unedited is read again and checked against Z1's stored none read. Shares per stratum (fact-first, fact-after; all beside) with 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals over the original bridge entity (10,000 resamples, seed 0; every arm and both readers on the same draws). (i): rise = S_K(whole_bL) - S_K(whole_1L) on fact-after, clause at >= 0.30; fact-first |S_K(whole_bL) - S_M(whole_bL)| <= 0.10 (the recall under the same arm); "the slice explanation" iff both; Q51.7 (i) reads the rise clause. (ii): extra loss = X0's excess (S_rand_bL - S_no_jpp_bL) / S_whole_bL per reader, gap = M's - K's on paired draws, labels as written, fact-first decisive, fact-after and all reported, Z1's one-layer cells beside; an undefined extra loss (no switch under whole_bL) holds no clause ("can't tell"). (iii): S_K(whole_bL) on fact-after < 0.50 -> "the link is made away from the bridge token" and the window read is reported. The window read is cheap, so it is recorded in every run (not a separate stage) and the verdict reports it only when (iii)'s condition holds: K reader, the first 50 fact-after passages in Z1's order, the patch token and both bridges' fact sentences (O's bridge's and S's bridge's true-fact sentences in the K passage; a sentence before the pointer has the same states in O and S, so patching it is a no-op) set to S's states at blocks 0..12; S_K(window) beside S_K(whole_bL) on the same 50. Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9 at the bars). Plain-text loss per arm and reader (descriptive): -log p(O's own next token) at the patch token, O's prompt cut after it, under none, Z1's three one-layer arms (recomputed: Z1 stored no loss), the three before-L arms and whole_emb; mean with intervals and its ratio to the one-layer whole's. Scored by hand after Q51.7 is committed: scripts/x51_carrier.py verdict.
controls: the J++ part of each layer's change against a random part of its own share at the same layers (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + l)
the recall (M) on the same passages and the same counterfactual (the gap)
Z1's one-layer arms on the same passages (stored rows), and O unedited read again against Z1's stored none read
Z1's read gate (0.80 per reader) and both readers right on O and S (its eligibility)
the plain-text loss per arm (collateral damage at the patch token)
whole_emb (the patch token's id swapped too) beside whole_bL; the whole before-L split by whether only the name's last token differs between O and S (descriptive)

At this scale a recall own-IIA below 0.5 at k = 128 is a result (no low-dimensional recall subspace at this token and layer), and the lookup subspace's energy says which named code the lookup reads.

One R per reader and k (lookup k 4, 16; recall 4, 16, 64, 128), R_pos per k (2, 4, 8); an untrained random R per k and an R trained on shuffled targets per R (48.1's and 49.8's seeds). decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.8; per model, the rest descriptive). l_J = the first layer from which the lookup's extra loss without J++ stays <= 0.10; l_P = the first layer where the position share under the whole change is >= 0.20; l_probe = the first layer where the slot probe is >= 0.80. (a) Handoff: l_P >= l_J, report l_P - l_J (Q35.1's failure on the 27B predicts a gap of about 4 layers there). (b) The address forms before it is used: l_probe <= l_P on every model; if the probe reaches 0.80 only after l_P, say so. (e) The recall side: the layer window where the whole change switches the recall >= 0.5, and whether without-J++ costs it >= 0.3 throughout that window (the recall's own onset layer reported beside l_J). decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch52.yaml brief B, Dan 29 Oct 00:30), verbatim: "Rules, fixed in advance. “Readable”: the answer word in the lens top-5 on ≥ 0.5 of items at some layer before the answer layer. “Usable”: writing its directions changes the answer on ≥ 0.3 of items with the random control ≤ 0.10. As computed (fixed before any run): the answer word = 51.12's (scripts/x51_answer.py word_ids: main the number word's one-letter-token variants, 'six' for 6; Z2 the first token of the answer word and its variants), its lens rank = 1 + tokens with a strictly higher J++ readout logit (JLens.readout, full vocabulary; the best variant), on the reader's O prompt; top-5 = rank <= 5; per cell (token group x layer) the share over the items that have that position. Token groups: main B = the bridge word (X0's position), E = the bridge entity's last mention before it (its locker sentence; 100 / 101 / 92 of 200 items have one), Q = the question's 'pick' token (51.10's P2), T = the appended space token (51.10's P3); Z2 B = the description's last token (his edit site), E = the bridge's name in the passage, Q = the question's closing '?', T = the prompt's last token. Layers: every second layer L0 through n_layers - 2 (those in the lens's source layers). Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9); cluster-bootstrap CIs over the bridge entity (10,000, seed 0) beside. Beside (not in the rules): the bridge entity's ranks (51.12's bridge rank), S's answer word on O (same-type distractor baseline), whole-word variants only (no 'G' for 'Greece', no 'I' for 'Iota'), the digit as read, the plain logit lens's answer-word rank, the frequency-matched write, the whole-state patch at the cell, 51.10's settle layer, and a check against 51.12's readout at the bridge word at X0's L (same items and token sets: top-50 0.14 / 0.07 / 0.00 lookup, 0.28 / 0.12 / 0.01 recall; Z2 9B / 27B ~0.53-0.62).

Order groups: x45m's (locker-first = the bridge's and S's bridge's locker sentences both before the asked pick; locker-after = both after). Both readers; their prompts differ from the question on, so S's states are taken per reader (one unedited forward of S and of O per reader and item, the read's space token appended). Layers: 0, 4, ..., 60, 62 (every 4th; the last block's output is read by nothing). Cells: S's block-l output set (exp04's SetRows, not added) into O at one token group, O's own tokens; token groups by character overlap in the rendered prompt: bridge (the bridge word); pick_rest (the asked pick sentence without the bridge and the person); person (the asked person's token); per locker sentence its item token(s) and its number token(s), the sentences named by role (lk_org = O's bridge's, lk_cf = S's bridge's: the added one in the clean design, the other person's original pick's in the main test; lk_other1, lk_other2 = the rest in context order); question (from the question's first token to the end of the prompt, the template's closing tokens and 'Answer:' included); last (the read position, the appended space token). The bridge is the only group whose token id differs between O and S; its row has one more cell, emb = O's prompt with S's token at the bridge and no state placed (the input embedding; block 0's input as a layer). Every other group's tokens are identical in O and S, and S's state there still differs downstream of the bridge: a cell measures what those tokens have read. In the main test the other person's changed pick is in no group; S's states at every group after it carry it too (it is what 47.4's (d)->100% measured), and in main items where that pick comes first the b margin and the bridge cells differ from the clean design's by it. Margins: b<l> = the bridge swapped at every layer <= l (blocks 0..l and its input embedding), one per sampled l; d = the whole asked pick sentence swapped at every layer (and the bridge's embedding). D2: w<l> = S's state set at the bridge at every block output >= l (O's tokens; the complement of b), one per sampled l; l_R per reader = the first sampled l at which the w curve is <= 0.1 (none: not reached). Beside them: none (O unedited), a (47.4's (a): h_S - h_O added at the bridge at L; X0's whole arm) and S read on S. Cell value = the switch rate over the order group's items (X0's chat read; switch = the top token is S's answer's first token), 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals over bridge items (10,000, seed 0, every arm on the same draws). Rules on point estimates: (a) every bridge cell (emb and every sampled layer) <= 0.25 and some lk_* item or number cell at any layer >= 0.5, on the lookup's locker-after map; (b) the last sampled layer with the lookup's bridge cell >= 0.3 is earlier than the recall's by >= 2 on the 9B (>= 4 on Muse and the 27B), locker-first; a reader with no such layer: the rule does not hold; (c) the recall's lk_cf item cell >= 0.3 at some layer in locker-first and < 0.3 at every layer in locker-after; D2: l_R(recall) over all the design's items <= 26 on the 9B (52 on the 27B; Muse has no band: reported). Each rule is scored on each design; the Q-depth answer per model reads the clean design (one token differs; its b, d and w0 arms are S's own run by construction), the main test beside it. Consequences of the design stated before the data: in the clean design the emb cell, every b<l>, d and w0 equal S read on S; in main items whose other changed pick comes after the asked one, b<l> at the last layer equals d. 47.4's state check stays: under the bridge swap at blocks 0..L the bridge's state after L must be S's (relative distance <= 0.05) on items whose O and S agree before the bridge, else the job fails after writing its files.
